            text: Does any part of the Harbor Pay acquisition migration need legal
              review before the Nov 15 close?
            revision: legacy:6abf4a45ae87313af8db04b89d546e0e1a1c6137341b3d3c0d159c66cf64d54c
            dossier_revision: 6d4914a844763bdf7319b43938d045b749a6c509b5e5a32e66d165707af39d26

          issue:
            issue_id: ISS-c9d7c39f63-d22ea3957f21252a
            title: Open alerts, suspicious activity history, and acquisition diligence
            why_it_matters: About 40 open alerts and several suspicious activity reports
              remain unreviewed. Their contents could affect the acquisition decision,
              deal protections, remediation, and account migration.
            parent_issue_id: null
            fact_ids: []
          facts:
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-182bcc
            text: Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15 (~10
              weeks out).
            source_ids:
            - REQ-20260909-283892
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-551367
            text: Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into
              Mosaic Relay's app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account and
              balance and full access to Mosaic's product set.
            source_ids:
            - REQ-20260909-283892
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-9a0c61
            text: Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC'd by Harbor.
            source_ids:
            - REQ-20260909-283892
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-33293c
            text: Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states; Mosaic
              Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening four new markets.
            source_ids:
            - REQ-20260909-283892
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-aea8ec
            text: Harbor's KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; Mosaic
              has pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying documents
              for users onboarded before 2023.
            source_ids:
            - REQ-20260909-283892
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-073838
            text: Harbor's transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
              terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor's transaction feed at
              Mosaic's engine on day 1.
            source_ids:
            - REQ-20260909-283892
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-19aebc
            text: Marketing wants a 'Welcome' campaign with a $50 bonus on first transfer,
              launching close+1.
            source_ids:
            - REQ-20260909-283892
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-adf2cb
            text: Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and 'a handful' of SARs from the
              last year at Harbor; nobody has read them yet.
            source_ids:
            - REQ-20260909-283892
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-4c1fd8
            text: Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into
              Mosaic Relay's app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account and
              balance.
            source_ids:
            - MSG-20260909-9835ba
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-f2c49f
            text: Plan is no re-verification of Harbor's existing KYC; Harbor users
              were already KYC'd.
            source_ids:
            - MSG-20260909-9835ba
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-13d4c1
            text: Harbor's KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail
              results exist for everyone but underlying documents are missing for
              users onboarded before 2023.
            source_ids:
            - MSG-20260909-9835ba
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-78d5cd
            text: Harbor's transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
              terminates at close; plan is to repoint the transaction feed to Mosaic
              Relay's engine on day 1.
            source_ids:
            - MSG-20260909-9835ba
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-9f7bde
            text: Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and 'a handful' of SARs from the
              last year at Harbor; none have been read yet.
            source_ids:
            - MSG-20260909-9835ba
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-ed9f06
            text: How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase (Mosaic
              buys Harbor's assets)
            source_ids:
            - MSG-20260909-2e549e
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-b5e71e
            text: Does Mosaic Relay's AML/CIP program currently permit relying on
              another institution's prior KYC without re-verification, or is re-verification
              required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance
            source_ids:
            - MSG-20260909-2e549e
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-849b00
            text: What is known about Harbor's ~40 open alerts and the SARs from the
              last year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence
            source_ids:
            - MSG-20260909-2e549e
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-f0fb01
            text: For the four new markets opened by the combined footprint, does
              Mosaic Relay plan to operate under Harbor's existing licenses or apply
              for its own? — Use/assume Harbor's licenses
            source_ids:
            - MSG-20260909-2e549e
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-620c62
            text: For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents,
              what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay's own BSA/AML customer identification
              and recordkeeping obligations? — It is not yet known whether Mosaic
              Relay's AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor's prior KYC; compliance
              must confirm.
            source_ids:
            - MSG-20260909-2e549e
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-070aec
            text: Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last year
              been reviewed, and what did they reveal? — The open alerts and SAR history
              have not been reviewed and remain in diligence.
            source_ids:
            - MSG-20260909-2e549e
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-771ee1
            text: For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint,
              what is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval
              before onboarding those customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans to
              use or assume Harbor's licenses for the four new markets.
            source_ids:
            - MSG-20260909-2e549e
          assumptions:
          - assumption_id: ASM-20260909-29b823
            text: Mosaic Relay's existing money transmission licenses and Harbor's
              MTLs are transferable or can be maintained through the acquisition without
              new state approval
            reason: Needed to continue
          - assumption_id: ASM-20260909-3c5756
            text: The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy Mosaic Relay's
              own BSA/AML program obligations without the underlying documents
            reason: Needed to continue
          - assumption_id: ASM-20260909-1a519f
            text: The transaction monitoring repoint can be completed and validated
              before close without a monitoring gap
            reason: Needed to continue
          - assumption_id: ASM-20260909-ca7dfd
            text: Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject to state MTL
              regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).
            reason: Needed to continue
          - assumption_id: ASM-20260909-d40239
            text: Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter in 41 states
              (per the request).
            reason: Needed to continue
          - assumption_id: ASM-20260909-57e86b
            text: The acquisition is structured as an asset or stock purchase, which
              affects whether Harbor's licenses and SAR/alert obligations transfer
              (structure not yet confirmed).
            reason: Needed to continue
          questions:
          - question_id: Q-SAR
            text: Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last year
              been reviewed, and what did they reveal?
            consequence: Unread open alerts and SARs are the highest-risk item; they
              can create BSA/AML exposure that must be addressed before close and
              could affect the deal itself.
            state: answered
            answer: The open alerts and SAR history have not been reviewed and remain
              in diligence.
            answer_kind: reported_fact
            linked_fact_ids:
            - FACT-20260909-070aec
          - question_id: Q-KYC
            text: For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents,
              what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay's own BSA/AML customer identification
              and recordkeeping obligations?
            consequence: Whether the missing underlying documents create a compliance
              gap depends on how Mosaic plans to satisfy its own CIP/recordkeeping
              obligations for these users.
            state: answered
            answer: It is not yet known whether Mosaic Relay's AML/CIP program permits
              reliance on Harbor's prior KYC; compliance must confirm.
            answer_kind: reported_fact
            linked_fact_ids:
            - FACT-20260909-620c62
          - question_id: Q-MTL
            text: For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint,
              what is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval
              before onboarding those customers?
            consequence: Whether the four new markets can be served at close depends
              on license transferability and state approval, which is a gating regulatory
              question.
            state: answered
            answer: Mosaic Relay currently plans to use or assume Harbor's licenses
              for the four new markets.
            answer_kind: reported_fact
            linked_fact_ids:
            - FACT-20260909-771ee1
          - question_id: Q-BONUS
            text: How is the $50 welcome bonus structured?
            consequence: The structure determines whether the bonus triggers consumer
              disclosure, funds-flow, or state promotional requirements.
            state: left_open
            answer: null
            answer_kind: null
            linked_fact_ids: []

              "content": "## Working position\n\nThe Harbor Pay migration needs legal

              is that an asset purchase generally requires Mosaic Relay to confirm
              its own authority to operate in each state; the current plan to use
              or assume Harbor''s licenses is not established as legally effective.\n\nThe
              second concern is BSA/AML readiness. Mosaic Relay has not confirmed
              whether its AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor''s prior KYC,
              and underlying records are missing for some pre-2023 users. Harbor''s
              open alerts and SAR history also remain unread. These gaps make a day-one
              migration without re-verification or account restrictions difficult
              to support.\n\nTransaction monitoring continuity is also material because
              Harbor''s vendor ends at close. The repointed feed should be tested
              and validated before migrated users receive full access. The $50 bonus
              is lower priority but still needs review once its eligibility, funding,
              terms, and disclosures are known.\n\n## Plausible alternatives\n\nA
              narrower launch could exclude the four new markets, restrict users whose
              KYC evidence is incomplete, or delay full product access until alert
              review and monitoring validation finish. A full day-one launch remains

              and monitoring continuity are confirmed.\n\n## Material facts and assumptions\n\nReported
              facts include the asset-purchase structure, the current plan to rely

              conduct regulated money-transmission activity and that Mosaic Relay
              will become the operating provider immediately after close. It does
              not assume that Harbor''s licenses transfer or that Harbor''s KYC is
              sufficient.\n\n## What could change this view\n\nThe view could change

              shows no monitoring gap. The bonus structure remains unknown.\n\n##

              "text": "14 \n \nARTICLE V \nMoney Transmission Licenses \nSection 5.01
              License Required. \n(a) \nA person may not engage in the business of
              money transmission or \nadvertise, solicit, or hold itself out as providing
              money transmission unless the person is licensed \nunder this [Act];
              \n(b) \n[Section 5.01(a)] does not apply to: \n(1) \nA person that is
              an authorized delegate of a person licensed under \nthis [Act] acting
              within the scope of authority conferred by a written contract with the
              \nlicensee; or \n(2) \nA person that is exempt pursuant to [Section
              3.01] and does not \nengage in money transmission outside the scope
              of such exemption. \n(c) \nA license issued under [Section 5.05] is
              not transferable or assignable. \nSection 5.02 Consistent State Licensing.
              \n(a) \nTo establish consistent licensing between [this state] and other
              states, the \n[Commissioner] is authorized and encouraged to: \n(1)
              \nimplement all licensing provisions of this [Act] in a manner that
              is \nconsistent with other states that have adopted this [Act]or multistate
              licensing processes; \nand \n(2) \nparticipate in nationwide protocols
              for licensing cooperation and \ncoordination among state regulators
              provided that such protocols are consistent with this \n[Act]. \n(b)
              \nIn order to fulfill the purposes of this [Act], the [Commissioner]
              is \nauthorized and encouraged to establish relationships or contracts
              with NMLS or other entities \ndesignated by NMLS to enable the [Commissioner]
              to: \n(1) \ncollect and maintain records; \n(2) \ncoordinate multistate
              licensing processes and supervision processes; \n(3) \nprocess fees;
              and \n(4) \nfacilitate communication between [state] and licensees or
              other \npersons subject to this [Act]. \n(c) \nThe [Commissioner] is
              authorized and encouraged to utilize NMLS for all \naspects of licensing
              in accordance with this [Act], including but not limited to, license
              applications, \napplications for acquisitions of control, surety bonds,
              reporting, criminal history background\n"}], "support_state": "retrieved",

              in information submitted by the licensee in its original license \napplication
              which has not been reported to the [Commissioner]. \n(c) \nThe [Commissioner]
              for good cause may grant an extension of the renewal \ndate. \n(d) \nThe
              [Commissioner] is authorized and encouraged to utilize NMLS to \nprocess
              license renewals provided that such functionality is consistent with
              this [Section 5.06]. \nSection 5.07 Maintenance of License. \n(a) \nIf
              a licensee does not continue to meet the qualifications or satisfy the
              \nrequirements that apply to an applicant for a new money transmission
              license, the [Commissioner] \nmay suspend or revoke the licensee''s
              license in accordance with the procedures established by this \n[Act]
              or other applicable state law for such suspension or revocation. \n(b)
              \nAn applicant for a money transmission license must demonstrate that
              it \nmeets or will meet, and a money transmission licensee must at all
              times meet, the requirements in \n[Sections 10.01, 10.02, and 10.03]
              of this [Act]. \nARTICLE VI \nAcquisition of Control and Change of Key
              Individual \nSection 6.01 Acquisition of Control. \n(a) \nAny person,
              or group of persons acting in concert, seeking to acquire control \nof
              a licensee shall obtain the written approval of the [Commissioner] prior
              to acquiring control. \nAn individual is not deemed to acquire control
              of a licensee and is not subject to these acquisition \nof control provisions
              when that individual becomes a key individual in the ordinary course
              of \nbusiness. \n(b) \nA person, or group of persons acting in concert,
              seeking to acquire control \nof a licensee shall, in cooperation with
              the licensee: \n(1) \nSubmit an application in a form and in a medium
              prescribed by the \n[Commissioner]; and \n(2) \nSubmit a nonrefundable
              fee of [$X] with the request for approval. \n(c) \nUpon request, the
              [Commissioner] may permit a licensee or the person, or \ngroup of persons
              acting in concert, to submit some or all information required by the
              \n[Commissioner] pursuant to [Section 6.01(b)(1)] without using NMLS.
              \n(d) \nThe application required by [Section 6.01(b)(1)] shall include
              information \nrequired by [Section 5.04] for any new key individuals
              that have not previously completed the \nrequirements of [Section 5.04]
              for a licensee.\n"}], "support_state": "retrieved", "url": "https://www.csbs.org/sites/default/files/2023-02/CSBS%20Money%20Transmission%20Modernization%20Act.pdf",
              "original_path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/sources/RUN-20260911-d08e84-37ee676da5b354ba8538-fetch.md.bin",
              "path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000021.md",
              "source_hash": "5638ae03ab2c6c110a80e30639b8ccd42a1c585fdc2818a38e4f2f0fc69a5e06",
              "source_label": "[PDF] CSBS Money Transmission Modernization Act — Page
              21, characters 0–2389", "unit_id": "p000021", "locator": "Page 21, characters
              0–2389", "available_excerpt": "21 \n \nin a medium prescribed by the
              [Commissioner]. The renewal report must state or contain a \ndescription
              of each material change in information submitted by the licensee in
              its original license \napplication which has not been reported to the
              [Commissioner]. \n(c) \nThe [Commissioner] for good cause may grant
              an extension of the renewal \ndate. \n(d) \nThe [Commissioner] is authorized
              and encouraged to utilize NMLS to \nprocess license renewals provided
              that such functionality is consistent with this [Section 5.06]. \nSection
              5.07 Maintenance of License. \n(a) \nIf a licensee does not continue
              to meet the qualifications or satisfy the \nrequirements that apply
              to an applicant for a new money transmission license, the [Commissioner]
              \nmay suspend or revoke the licensee''s license in accordance with the
              procedures established by this \n[Act] or other applicable state law
              for such suspension or revocation. \n(b) \nAn applicant for a money
              transmission license must demonstrate that it \nmeets or will meet,
              and a money transmission licensee must at all times meet, the requirements
              in \n[Sections 10.01, 10.02, and 10.03] of this [Act]. \nARTICLE VI
              \nAcquisition of Control and Change of Key Individual \nSection 6.01
              Acquisition of Control. \n(a) \nAny person, or group of persons acting
              in concert, seeking to acquire control \nof a licensee shall obtain
              the written approval of the [Commissioner] prior to acquiring control.
              \nAn individual is not deemed to acquire control of a licensee and is
              not subject to these acquisition \nof control provisions when that individual
              becomes a key individual in the ordinary course of \nbusiness. \n(b)
              \nA person, or group of persons acting in concert, seeking to acquire
              control \nof a licensee shall, in cooperation with the licensee: \n(1)
              \nSubmit an application in a form and in a medium prescribed by the
              \n[Commissioner]; and \n(2) \nSubmit a nonrefundable fee of [$X] with
              the request for approval. \n(c) \nUpon request, the [Commissioner] may
              permit a licensee or the person, or \ngroup of persons acting in concert,
              to submit some or all information required by the \n[Commissioner] pursuant
              to [Section 6.01(b)(1)] without using NMLS. \n(d) \nThe application
              required by [Section 6.01(b)(1)] shall include information \nrequired
              by [Section 5.04] for any new key individuals that have not previously
              completed the \nrequirements of [Section 5.04] for a licensee.\n"},
              {"source_id": "SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538", "source_version": "dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a",
              "title": "[PDF] CSBS Money Transmission Modernization Act", "extraction_state":
              "complete", "selected_passages": [{"unit_id": "p000022", "start": 0,
              "end": 2612, "page_number": 22, "section_label": null, "body_hash":
              "175b57e812c71a8532569030d2db7113b5adc94e61bd9922dc0fee5d833c2748",
              "path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000022.md",
              "text": "22 \n \n(e) \nWhen an application for acquisition of control
              under this [Section 6.01] \nappears to include all the items and address
              all of the matters that are required, the application shall \nbe considered
              complete and the [Commissioner] shall promptly notify the applicant
              in a record of \nthe date on which the application was determined to
              be complete and:15 \n \n(1) \nThe [Commissioner] shall approve or deny
              the application within 60 \ndays after the completion date; or \n(2)
              \nif the application is not approved or denied within 60 days after
              the \ncompletion date: \n(A) \nthe application is approved; and \n(B)
              \nthe person, or group of persons acting in concert, are not \nprohibited
              from acquiring control. \n(3) \nThe [Commissioner] may for good cause
              extend the application \nperiod. \n(f) \nA determination by the [Commissioner]
              that an application is complete and \nis accepted for processing means
              only that the application, on its face, appears to include all of the
              \nitems and address all of the matters that are required, and is not
              an assessment of the substance of \nthe application or of the sufficiency
              of the information provided. \n(g) \nWhen an application is filed and
              considered complete under [Section \n6.01(e)], the [Commissioner] shall
              investigate the financial condition and responsibility, financial \nand
              business experience, character, and general fitness of the person, or
              group of persons acting in \nconcert, seeking to acquire control. The
              [Commissioner] shall approve an acquisition of control \npursuant to
              this [Section 6.01] if the [Commissioner] finds that all of the following
              conditions have \nbeen fulfilled: \n(1) \nThe requirements of subsections
              (b) and (d) have been met, as \napplicable; and \n(2) \nthe financial
              condition and responsibility, financial and business \nexperience, competence,
              character, and general fitness of the person, or group of persons \nacting
              in concert, seeking to acquire control; and the competence, experience,
              character, \nand general fitness of the key individuals and persons
              that would be in control of the \nlicensee after the acquisition of
              control indicate that it is in the interest of the public to \npermit
              the person, or group of persons acting in concert, to control the licensee.
              \n(h) \nIf an applicant avails itself or is otherwise subject to a multistate
              licensing \n \n15 Commentary: NMLS will accommodate and streamline the
              process of communicating when applications are \nreceived and when states
              consider them to have been complete. The intent of this Act is for the
              application period to \nbegin on the day an application is determined
              to be complete.\n"}], "support_state": "retrieved", "url": "https://www.csbs.org/sites/default/files/2023-02/CSBS%20Money%20Transmission%20Modernization%20Act.pdf",

              "source_hash": "175b57e812c71a8532569030d2db7113b5adc94e61bd9922dc0fee5d833c2748",

              that would be in control of the \nlicensee after the acquisition of

              the person, or group of persons acting in concert, to control the licensee.
              \n(h) \nIf an applicant avails itself or is otherwise subject to a multistate

              process of communicating when applications are \nreceived and when states
              consider them to have been complete. The intent of this Act is for the
              application period to \nbegin on the day an application is determined

              "dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a", "title": "[PDF] CSBS Money Transmission
              Modernization Act", "extraction_state": "complete", "selected_passages":
              [{"unit_id": "p000023", "start": 0, "end": 2523, "page_number": 23,
              "section_label": null, "body_hash": "83a664c778fbc9de0b4d13270e2a918f6488b461db1a6617e3d36032163068ca",
              "path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000023.md",
              "text": "23 \n \nprocess: \n(1) \nthe [Commissioner] is authorized and
              encouraged to accept the \ninvestigation results of a lead investigative
              state for the purpose of [Section 6.01(g)] if the \nlead investigative
              state has sufficient staffing, expertise, and minimum standards; or
              \n(2) \nif [state] is a lead investigative state, the [Commissioner]
              is \nauthorized and encouraged to investigate the applicant pursuant
              to [Section 6.01(g)] and \nthe timeframes established by agreement through
              the multistate licensing process. \n(i) \nThe [Commissioner] shall issue
              a formal written notice of the denial of an \napplication to acquire
              control within thirty (30) days of the decision to deny the application.
              The \n[Commissioner] shall set forth in the notice of denial the specific
              reasons for the denial of the \napplication. An applicant whose application
              is denied by the [Commissioner] under this [Section \n6.01(i)] may appeal
              within thirty (30) days16 after receipt of the written notice of the
              denial \n[pursuant to state administrative law procedures]. \n(j) \nThe
              requirements of [Section 6.01(a) and (b)] do not apply to any of the
              \nfollowing: \n(1) \nA person that acts as a proxy for the sole purpose
              of voting at a \ndesignated meeting of the shareholders or holders of
              voting shares or voting interests of a \nlicensee or a person in control
              of a licensee; \n(2) \nA person that acquires control of a licensee
              by devise or descent; \n(3) \nA person that acquires control of a licensee
              as a personal \nrepresentative, custodian, guardian, conservator, or
              trustee, or as an officer appointed by a \ncourt of competent jurisdiction
              or by operation of law; \n(4) \nA person that is exempt under [Section
              3.01(g)]; \n(5) \nA person that the [Commissioner] determines is not
              subject to \n[Section 6.01(a)] based on the public interest; \n(6) \nA
              public offering of securities of a licensee or a person in control of
              \na licensee; or \n(7) \nAn internal reorganization of a person in control
              of the licensee \nwhere the ultimate person in control of the licensee
              remains the same. \n(k) \nPersons in [Sections 6.01(j)(2), (3), (4),
              (6), (7)] in cooperation with the \nlicensee shall notify the [Commissioner]
              within [15] days after the acquisition of control.17 \n \n16 Commentary:
              Administrative procedures for challenging a departmental decision may
              be derived from other \naspects of state law. In such a case, this Act
              should be adjusted to reflect the relevant administrative process. \n17
              Commentary: Notice is satisfied upon updating the licensee’s NMLS record.\n"}],
              "support_state": "retrieved", "url": "https://www.csbs.org/sites/default/files/2023-02/CSBS%20Money%20Transmission%20Modernization%20Act.pdf",

              notify the [Commissioner] within [15] days after the acquisition of

              law. In such a case, this Act should be adjusted to reflect the relevant
              administrative process. \n17 Commentary: Notice is satisfied upon updating
              the licensee’s NMLS record.\n"}, {"source_id": "SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538",

              CSBS Money Transmission Modernization Act", "extraction_state": "complete",
              "selected_passages": [{"unit_id": "p000024", "start": 0, "end": 2799,
              "page_number": 24, "section_label": null, "body_hash": "4732d9c2b053975a4d3cb27db8e99faa4baf45f71eb350fa519e31b5890ac680",
              "path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000024.md",
              "text": "24 \n \n(l) \nStreamlined Acquisition of Control \n(1) \nThe
              requirements of [Section 6.01(a) and (b)] do not apply to a \nperson
              that has complied with and received approval to engage in money transmission
              \nunder this [Act] or was identified as a person in control in a prior
              application filed with and \napproved by the [Commissioner] or by an
              MSB accredited state pursuant to a multistate \nlicensing process, provided
              that: \n(A) \nthe person has not had a license revoked or suspended
              or \ncontrolled a licensee that has had a license revoked or suspended
              while the person \nwas in control of the licensee in the previous 5-years;
              \n(B) \nif the person is a licensee, the person is well managed and
              \nhas received at least a satisfactory rating for compliance at its
              most recent \nexamination by an MSB accredited state if such rating
              was given; \n(C) \nthe licensee to be acquired is projected to meet
              the \nrequirements of [Sections 10.01, 10.02, and 10.03] of this [Act]
              after the acquisition \nof control is completed, and if the person acquiring
              control is a licensee, that \nlicensee is also projected to meet the
              requirements of [Sections 10.01, 10.02, and \n10.03] of this [Act] after
              the acquisition of control is completed; \n(D) \nthe licensee to be
              acquired will not implement any material \nchanges to its business plan
              as a result of the acquisition of control, and if the person \nacquiring
              control is a licensee, that licensee also will not implement any material
              \nchanges to its business plan as a result of the acquisition of control;  and
              \n(E) \nthe person provides notice of the acquisition in cooperation
              \nwith the licensee and attests to [Section 6.01(l)(1)(A), (B), (C),
              and (D)] in a form \nand in a medium prescribed by the [Commissioner].
              \n(2) \nIf the notice is not disapproved within 30 days after the date
              on \nwhich the notice was determined to be complete, the notice is deemed
              approved. \n(m) \nBefore filing an application for approval to acquire
              control of a licensee a \nperson may request in writing a determination
              from the [Commissioner] as to whether the person \nwould be considered
              a person in control of a licensee upon consummation of a proposed \ntransaction.
              If the [Commissioner] determines that the person would not be a person
              in control of \na licensee, the proposed Person and transaction is not
              subject to the requirements of [Section \n6.01(a) and (b)] of this [Act].
              \n(n) \nIf a multistate licensing process includes a determination pursuant
              to \n[Section 6.01(m)] and an applicant avails itself or is otherwise
              subject to the multistate licensing \nprocess: \n(1) \nThe [Commissioner]
              is authorized and encouraged to accept the \ncontrol determination of
              a lead investigative state with sufficient staffing, expertise, and
              \nminimum standards for the purpose of [Section 6.01(m)]; or\n"}], "support_state":

              "text": "ly for goods or services provided by the issuer or its affiliate
              or franchisees of the issuer \nor its affiliate, except to the extent

              \n(f) \n\"Control\" means \n(1) \n(A) the power to vote, directly or
              indirectly, at least 25 percent of \nthe outstanding voting shares or
              voting interests of a licensee or person in control of a \nlicensee;
              \n(B) \nthe power to elect or appoint a majority of key individuals
              or \nexecutive officers, managers, directors, trustees, or other persons
              exercising \nmanagerial authority of a person in control of a licensee;
              or \n(C) \nthe power to exercise, directly or indirectly, a controlling
              \ninfluence over the management or policies of a licensee or person
              in control of a \nlicensee. \n(2) \nRebuttable Presumption of Control.
              \n(A) \nA person is presumed to exercise a controlling influence \nwhen
              the person holds the power to vote, directly or indirectly, at least
              10 percent \nof the outstanding voting shares or voting interests of
              a licensee or person in control \nof a licensee.2 \n(B) \nA person presumed
              to exercise a controlling influence as \ndefined by this [Section 2.01(f)]
              can rebut the presumption of control if the person \nis a passive investor.
              \n(3) \nFor purposes of determining the percentage of a person controlled
              \nby any other person, the person''s interest shall be aggregated with
              the interest of any other \nimmediate family member, including the person''s
              spouse, parents, children, siblings, \nmothers- and fathers-in law,
              sons- and daughters-in-law, brothers- and sisters-in-law, and \nany
              other person who shares such person''s home. \n(g) \n\"Eligible rating\"
              shall mean a credit rating of any of the three highest rating \ncategories
              provided by an eligible rating service, whereby each category may include
              rating \n \n2 Commentary: The obligation to rebut control rests exclusively
              with the person acquiring ≥10% of the outstanding \nvoting shares or
              voting interests of a licensee or person in control of a licensee.  It
              is not the responsibility of the \nlicensee to rebut control.  This
              is consistent with Section 601(a) of the Act which requires the person
              acquiring control \nto obtain prior approval.\n"}], "support_state":

              "text": "30 \n \n(1) \nappoint the person signing the contract as the
              licensee''s authorized \ndelegate with the authority to conduct money
              transmission on behalf of the licensee; \n(2) \nset forth the nature
              and scope of the relationship between the \nlicensee and the authorized
              delegate and the respective rights and responsibilities of the \nparties;
              \n(3) \nrequire the authorized delegate to agree to fully comply with
              all \napplicable state and federal laws, rules, and regulations pertaining
              to money transmission, \nincluding this [Act] and regulations implementing
              this [Act], relevant provisions of the \nBank Secrecy Act and the USA
              PATRIOT ACT; \n(4) \nrequire the authorized delegate to remit and handle
              money and \nmonetary value in accordance with the terms of the contract
              between the licensee and the \nauthorized delegate; \n(5) \nimpose a
              trust on money and monetary value net of fees received for \nmoney transmission
              for the benefit of the licensee; \n(6) \nrequire the authorized delegate
              to prepare and maintain records as \nrequired by this [Act] or regulations
              implementing this [Act], or as reasonably requested \nby the [Commissioner];
              \n(7) \nacknowledge that the authorized delegate consents to examination
              \nor investigation by the [Commissioner]; \n(8) \nstate that the licensee
              is subject to regulation by the [Commissioner] \nand that, as part of
              that regulation, the [Commissioner] may suspend or revoke an \nauthorized
              delegate designation or require the licensee to terminate an authorized
              delegate \ndesignation; and \n(9) \n(9)  acknowledge receipt of the
              written policies and procedures \nrequired under [Section 8.01(b)(1)].
              \n(e) \nIf the licensee''s license is suspended, revoked, surrendered,
              or expired, the \nlicensee must, within five (5) business days, provide
              documentation to the [Commissioner] that \nthe licensee has notified
              all applicable authorized delegates of the licensee whose names are

              surrender, or expiration of a \nlicense. Upon suspension, revocation,
              surrender, or expiration of a license, applicable authorized \ndelegates
              shall immediately cease to provide money transmission as an authorized
              delegate of the \nlicensee. \n(f) \nAn authorized delegate of a licensee
              holds in trust for the benefit of the \nlicensee all money net of fees
              received from money transmission.  If any authorized delegate \ncommingles
              any funds received from money transmission with any other funds or property
              owned \nor controlled by the authorized delegate, all commingled funds
              and other property shall be \nconsidered held in trust in favor of the
              licensee in an amount equal to the amount of money net of\n"}], "support_state":

              Modernization Act", "extraction_state": "complete", "selected_passages":
              [{"unit_id": "p000031", "start": 0, "end": 2704, "page_number": 31,
              "section_label": null, "body_hash": "994d5382d8c2640923eca8c8aabbca98c8fbaeec037edafbf7675c1a3819b1e7",
              "path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000031.md",
              "text": "31 \n \nfees received from money transmission.22 \n(g) \nAn
              authorized delegate may not use a subdelegate to conduct money \ntransmission
              on behalf of a licensee. \nSection 8.02 Unauthorized Activities \nA
              person shall not engage in the business of money transmission on behalf
              of a person \nnot licensed under this [Act]  or not exempt pursuant
              to [Article III] of this [Act]. A person that \nengages in such activity
              provides money transmission to the same extent as if the person were
              a \nlicensee, and shall be jointly and severally liable with the unlicensed
              or nonexempt person. \nSection 8.03 [Optional]: Prohibited Authorized
              Delegates. \n(a) \nThe [appropriate court] in an action brought by a
              licensee shall have \njurisdiction to grant appropriate equitable or
              legal relief, including without limitation prohibiting \nthe authorized
              delegate from directly or indirectly acting as an authorized delegate
              for any licensee \nin this state and the payment of restitution, damages
              or other monetary relief, if the [appropriate \ncourt] finds that an
              authorized delegate failed to remit money in accordance with the written
              \ncontract required by [Section 8.01(b)] or as otherwise directed by
              the licensee or required by law. \n(b) \nIf the [appropriate court]
              issues an order prohibiting a person from acting as \nan authorized
              delegate for any licensee pursuant to [Section 8.03(a)], the licensee
              that brought the \naction shall report the order to the [Commissioner]
              within thirty (30) days and shall report the \norder through NMLS within
              ninety (90) days. \n(c) \nAn authorized delegate who holds money in
              trust for the benefit of a \nlicensee and knowingly fails to remit more
              than [$XXX] of such money is guilty of a [reference \nto state classification]
              felony. \n(d) \nAn authorized delegate who holds money in trust for
              the benefit of a \nlicensee and knowingly fails to remit no more than
              [$XXX] of such money is guilty of a [reference \nto state classification]
              misdemeanor. \nARTICLE IX  \nTimely Transmission, Refunds, and Disclosures
              \nSection 9.01 Timely Transmission. \n(a) \nEvery licensee shall forward
              all money received for transmission in \naccordance with the terms of
              the agreement between the licensee and the sender unless the licensee
              \nhas a reasonable belief or a reasonable basis to believe that the
              sender may be a victim of fraud or \nthat a crime or violation of law,
              rule, or regulation has occurred, is occurring, or may occur. \n(b)
              \nIf a licensee fails to forward money received for transmission in
              accordance \nwith this section, the licensee must respond to inquiries
              by the sender with the reason for the failure \n \n22 Commentary: An
              express trust account or segregated bank account is not required.\n"}],

              {"source_id": "SRC-71b20ecf65825d6522c4", "source_version": "d021ece0cde82565eb83511c8122c85b",
              "title": "Money Transmitter Licensing | Department of Financial Services",
              "extraction_state": "complete", "selected_passages": [{"unit_id": "s000001",
              "start": 2400, "end": 7324, "page_number": null, "section_label": "Section
              1", "body_hash": "3c6e0983ad889dc93334add58721659be3ac3d4bf1075f544bcd9c940396e471",
              "path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-71b20ecf65825d6522c4/d021ece0cde82565eb83511c8122c85b/sections/s000001.md",
              "text": "ey Transmitter License.\n\nAccess to NMLS\n\nNMLS is a secure
              web-based system created by state regulators to provide efficiencies
              in the processing of state licenses and improve supervision of state-regulated
              industries.\n\nTo access NMLS for the first time, you must complete
              a Company Account Request Form and identify a Primary Account Administrator
              and a Secondary Account Administrator. This form can be submitted online
              through the NMLS website in the Getting Started section. This form needs
              to be submitted only once per company, regardless of the number of NMLS
              participating states in which you are licensed.\n\nWithin three days
              of completing and submitting the Company Account Request Form, the Primary
              Account Administrator will receive NMLS login information. The Primary
              Account Administrator will have full rights to access the system, submit
              information to this agency and other participating state regulators,
              and set up other company users in the system. Instructions and tutorials
              on how to access and use the system are also available in the NMLS Resource
              Center .\n\nNote : If your company already has a record in NMLS, you
              can omit this step.\n\nManaging Your License on NMLS\n\nEach company
              holding a DFS Money Transmitter License who wishes to manage their license
              on NMLS must create a company record in the system. To gain access to
              NMLS, the applicant must submit a form requesting an NMLS account.\n\nCurrent
              New York State Money Transmitters may transition their licenses to NMLS.
              See the DFS Money Transmitter Transition Checklist for more information.\n\nSubmitting
              a Complete Application\n\nTo submit an application and ensure your application
              is received, acknowledged as complete, and processed, please follow
              the instructions on the DFS Money Transmitter Checklists . No application
              shall be deemed to be complete until the Department has received all
              required information, documents, and fees.\n\nIn the process of reviewing
              and considering the application, DFS may request additional information
              and supporting documents.\n\nIn the application process, an NMLS Identification
              Number will be assigned to your application. Please maintain a record
              of this NMLS Identification Number, as it will be used as your application
              reference number throughout the remainder of the application process.
              The applicant’s NMLS Identification Number must be included on every
              hard-copy document submitted to the Department.\n\nNote : If the applicant
              has already submitted Forms MU1 and MU2 through NMLS for another state,
              the applicant does not need to re-enter the company record into NMLS.
              However, the applicant is required to provide jurisdiction-specific
              information to support its New York State application.\n\nBack to Top
              ▲\n\nNext Section\n\nContinue\n\nAnnual Reporting\n\nThe Annual Report
              should be prepared by qualified persons and submitted within 120 days
              following the close of the calendar year January 1 to December 31, 2025.\n\n2025
              NMLS Money Transmitter Annual Report Form\n\n2025 Non-NMLS Money Transmitter
              Annual Report Form\n\nBack to Top ▲\n\nNext Section\n\nContinue\n\nReporting
              Change in Certain Individuals\n\nPursuant to the following sections
              of the New York Banking Law (BL) and Superintendent’s Regulations (SR),
              licensees of the Department of Financial Services (DFS) are required
              to notify the Superintendent of changes in certain individuals, within
              stipulated time frames:\n\nMoney Transmitters: BL 641, 642 and 652-a;
              and SR 406.11\n\nThese requirements are for changes in certain individuals
              of licensees whose licenses are not managed on NMLS. For those managed
              on NMLS, visit the NMLS section website for New York State and navigate
              to Company Licenses and Amendment under the pertinent industry type,
              and look under Change in Control on the Amendment Checklist.\n\nIncluded
              Individuals\n\nMembers of the governing board such as directors, trustees,
              and LLC members\n\nOfficers (at a minimum Chief Executive Officer, President,
              Chief Financial Officer, Chief Compliance Officer, and Chief Operations
              Officer, and any other officers deemed necessary by DFS)\n\nDocumentary
              requirements for Each Included Individual Being Added\n\nNotification
              on the licensee''s letterhead signed by an authorized officer containing
              the following:\n\nName and title of the individual being added\n\nEffective
              date of the addition\n\nName and title of the person being replaced,
              and his/her new title/position, if any\n\nResolution of the governing
              board approving the addition\n\nPersonal Questionnaire (PDF)\n\nFingerprints\n\nBackground
              Investigation Report *\n\nLitigation Affidavit (PDF)\n\nAuthority to
              Release Information (PDF)\n\nResume\n\nDocumentary requirements for
              Each Included Individual Being Removed:\n\nNotification on the licensee''s
              letterhead signed by an authorized officer containing the following:\n\nName
              and title of the individual being removed\n\nReason of the removal\n\nEffective
              date of the removal\n\nNew title/position, if any\n\nWhere To Submit?"}],
              "support_state": "retrieved", "url": "https://www.dfs.ny.gov/apps_and_licensing/money_transmitters",
              "original_path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/sources/RUN-20260911-d08e84-71b20ecf65825d6522c4-fetch.md.bin",

              "source_hash": "3c6e0983ad889dc93334add58721659be3ac3d4bf1075f544bcd9c940396e471",
              "source_label": "Money Transmitter Licensing | Department of Financial

              License.\n\nAccess to NMLS\n\nNMLS is a secure web-based system created
              by state regulators to provide efficiencies in the processing of state
              licenses and improve supervision of state-regulated industries.\n\nTo

              Request Form and identify a Primary Account Administrator and a Secondary
              Account Administrator. This form can be submitted online through the
              NMLS website in the Getting Started section. This form needs to be submitted
              only once per company, regardless of the number of NMLS participating
              states in which you are licensed.\n\nWithin three days of completing
              and submitting the Company Account Request Form, the Primary Account
              Administrator will receive NMLS login information. The Primary Account
              Administrator will have full rights to access the system, submit information
              to this agency and other participating state regulators, and set up
              other company users in the system. Instructions and tutorials on how
              to access and use the system are also available in the NMLS Resource
              Center .\n\nNote : If your company already has a record in NMLS, you
              can omit this step.\n\nManaging Your License on NMLS\n\nEach company
              holding a DFS Money Transmitter License who wishes to manage their license
              on NMLS must create a company record in the system. To gain access to
              NMLS, the applicant must submit a form requesting an NMLS account.\n\nCurrent
              New York State Money Transmitters may transition their licenses to NMLS.
              See the DFS Money Transmitter Transition Checklist for more information.\n\nSubmitting
              a Complete Application\n\nTo submit an application and ensure your application
              is received, acknowledged as complete, and processed, please follow
              the instructions on the DFS Money Transmitter Checklists . No application
              shall be deemed to be complete until the Department has received all
              required information, documents, and fees.\n\nIn the process of reviewing
              and considering the application, DFS may request additional information
              and supporting documents.\n\nIn the application process, an NMLS Identification
              Number will be assigned to your application. Please maintain a record
              of this NMLS Identification Number, as it will be used as your application
              reference number throughout the remainder of the application process.
              The applicant’s NMLS Identification Number must be included on every
              hard-copy document submitted to the Department.\n\nNote : If the applicant
              has already submitted Forms MU1 and MU2 through NMLS for another state,
              the applicant does not need to re-enter the company record into NMLS.
              However, the applicant is required to provide jurisdiction-specific
              information to support its New York State application.\n\nBack to Top
              ▲\n\nNext Section\n\nContinue\n\nAnnual Reporting\n\nThe Annual Report
              should be prepared by qualified persons and submitted within 120 days
              following the close of the calendar year January 1 to December 31, 2025.\n\n2025
              NMLS Money Transmitter Annual Report Form\n\n2025 Non-NMLS Money Transmitter
              Annual Report Form\n\nBack to Top ▲\n\nNext Section\n\nContinue\n\nReporting
              Change in Certain Individuals\n\nPursuant to the following sections
              of the New York Banking Law (BL) and Superintendent’s Regulations (SR),
              licensees of the Department of Financial Services (DFS) are required
              to notify the Superintendent of changes in certain individuals, within
              stipulated time frames:\n\nMoney Transmitters: BL 641, 642 and 652-a;
              and SR 406.11\n\nThese requirements are for changes in certain individuals
              of licensees whose licenses are not managed on NMLS. For those managed
              on NMLS, visit the NMLS section website for New York State and navigate
              to Company Licenses and Amendment under the pertinent industry type,
              and look under Change in Control on the Amendment Checklist.\n\nIncluded
              Individuals\n\nMembers of the governing board such as directors, trustees,
              and LLC members\n\nOfficers (at a minimum Chief Executive Officer, President,
              Chief Financial Officer, Chief Compliance Officer, and Chief Operations
              Officer, and any other officers deemed necessary by DFS)\n\nDocumentary
              requirements for Each Included Individual Being Added\n\nNotification
              on the licensee''s letterhead signed by an authorized officer containing
              the following:\n\nName and title of the individual being added\n\nEffective
              date of the addition\n\nName and title of the person being replaced,
              and his/her new title/position, if any\n\nResolution of the governing
              board approving the addition\n\nPersonal Questionnaire (PDF)\n\nFingerprints\n\nBackground
              Investigation Report *\n\nLitigation Affidavit (PDF)\n\nAuthority to
              Release Information (PDF)\n\nResume\n\nDocumentary requirements for
              Each Included Individual Being Removed:\n\nNotification on the licensee''s
              letterhead signed by an authorized officer containing the following:\n\nName
              and title of the individual being removed\n\nReason of the removal\n\nEffective
              date of the removal\n\nNew title/position, if any\n\nWhere To Submit?"},
              {"source_id": "SRC-b48d8d40f5a0cfe9a200", "source_version": "6ebc7b743e605b8e05363eb0628942c1",
              "title": "How To Get A Money Transmitter License (MTL) in the U.S. -
              Fenergo", "extraction_state": "complete", "selected_passages": [{"unit_id":
              "s000002", "start": 0, "end": 3321, "page_number": null, "section_label":
              "Section 2", "body_hash": "b8cfb71cc698f4b53cce08d023441fce54bf275adbcb1164dfb05a05143f6ba9",
              "path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-b48d8d40f5a0cfe9a200/6ebc7b743e605b8e05363eb0628942c1/sections/s000002.md",
              "text": "How To Get A Money Transmitter License (MTL) in the U.S.\n\nPublished
              Date  January 29, 2026\n\nTo get a Money Transmitter License (MTL),
              businesses must undergo a rigorous application process that involves
              dual compliance with federal (like FinCEN''s AML/KYC protocols) and
              varying state-level regulations. Key requirements across states include
              demonstrating financial viability, often requiring a surety bond and
              capital reserves, passing comprehensive background checks for key personnel,
              and establishing a robust internal compliance program. The process is
              complex, time-consuming, and mandates extensive documentation and financial
              disclosures to ensure the applicant is law-abiding and financially sound.\n\nOperating
              a money transfer service in the U.S. involves tackling a myriad of federal
              and state laws, making how to get a money transmitter license both time-consuming
              and expensive. Compliance with agencies like FinCEN is non-negotiable
              to prevent illegal activities.\n\nCompanies can either secure their
              own MSB license or partner with a licensed entity, but legal adherence
              is vital in both scenarios. It''s essential to understand what a money
              transmitter license is and who needs it.\n\nWhat is a Money Transmitter
              License?\n\nA Money Transmitter License is an official authorization
              or money service business license that empowers a firm or individual
              to facilitate the movement of capital. This license enables MSBs to
              handle financial transactions, ranging from digital payments to wire
              transfers.\n\nPossessing a Money Transmitter License brings forth substantial
              regulatory oversight. Organizations must prove they have the governance
              structure and internal controls to manage and safeguard client funds.
              States will continually scrutinize applicants, denying licensure to
              those who fail to meet the stringent criteria.\n\nIn the United States,
              the need for a Money Transmitter License is not a choice; it''s a requirement
              for virtually any business involved in the handling or transferring
              of funds. Money transmitter license requirements by state can vary,
              so it''s crucial to be aware of the respective state money transmitter
              regulations.\n\nHow to Get a Money Transmitter License?\n\nThe license
              application process is designed to be rigorous, ensuring that approved
              businesses are law-abiding and financially sound. Federal and state-level
              regulations diverge, with each state setting its own financial criteria
              and often requiring a minimum capital commitment.\n\nApplicants typically
              need a surety bond of at least $500,000 per state, with costs influenced
              by credit history. The duration to obtain the license varies, contingent
              on the business type and the state of operation.\n\nMoney Transmitter
              License Requirements\n\nAcquiring a money transmitter license involves
              compliance with Anti-Money Laundering (AML) and Know Your Customer (KYC)
              protocols. While these regulations are federal, individual states often
              impose additional requirements, thereby necessitating dual compliance.\n\nSubsequent
              to application submission, state authorities undertake an investigative
              review, focusing on financial sustainability and the applicant''s background.\n\nStandardized
              Requirements Across States\n\nRegistration: Initial registration typically
              occurs with the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network or a similar state-level
              body."}], "support_state": "retrieved", "url": "https://resources.fenergo.com/blogs/how-to-get-a-money-transmitter-license",

              "locator": "Section 2, characters 0–3321", "available_excerpt": "How

              regulations diverge, with each state setting its own financial criteria
              and often requiring a minimum capital commitment.\n\nApplicants typically
              need a surety bond of at least $500,000 per state, with costs influenced

              on the business type and the state of operation.\n\nMoney Transmitter
              License Requirements\n\nAcquiring a money transmitter license involves

              "e06621859d4ec9431f2712a7c357b112", "title": "OCC Confirms National
              Bank Act Preempts State Money Transmitter ...", "extraction_state":
              "complete", "selected_passages": [{"unit_id": "s000001", "start": 600,
              "end": 4794, "page_number": null, "section_label": "Section 1", "body_hash":
              "8ef30c0b98621db1f11c16332c16e9928ea8f237d6b055f645f7b449f18cbdfb",
              "path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-e6c1e4e85e004ccbe413/e06621859d4ec9431f2712a7c357b112/sections/s000001.md",
              "text": ", 2026\n\nPosted in Bank Regulatory\n\nOn May 12, the Office
              of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) issued a significant interpretive
              letter confirming that Fidelity Digital Assets, National Association
              (the recently converted national trust bank formerly known as Fidelity
              Digital Assets Service, LLC) is not required to hold state money transmitter
              licenses to conduct its federally authorized activities. The OCC concluded
              that the National Bank Act preempts any state money transmitter licensing
              requirement as applied to a national bank.\n\nUntil December 12, 2025,
              Fidelity Digital Assets operated as a New York-chartered limited liability
              trust company and held money transmitter licenses in numerous states,
              including Iowa. On that date, the OCC approved its conversion to an
              uninsured national trust bank under 12 U.S.C. § 27(a). Concurrent with
              the conversion, the Bank surrendered its Iowa money transmitter license.\n\nIowa
              pushed back. Its money transmitter statute exempts banks and trust companies
              from licensing, but only if they hold federally insured deposits. Because
              Fidelity Digital Assets is an uninsured national bank, Iowa argued the
              exemption did not apply and requested a legal basis for the license
              surrender. Fidelity Digital Assets responded that the National Bank
              Act preempts Iowa’s requirements and asked the OCC to confirm that position.\n\nThe
              OCC’s analysis of whether a state can require a national bank to obtain
              a state money transmitter license as a condition of engaging in federally
              authorized activities, including cryptocurrency custody, trade execution,
              stablecoin issuance, and related digital asset services, rested on two
              independent and well-established pillars of federal banking law:\n\n1.
              National Bank Act Preemption\n\nFederal law authorizes national banks
              to conduct a broad range of activities on a national basis. Any state
              law that “prevents or significantly interferes” with a national bank’s
              exercise of its federally authorized powers is preempted.\n\nThe OCC
              reasoned that requiring a national bank to obtain a state money transmitter
              license, even as a threshold condition to operating, would impermissibly
              condition the Bank’s federal authority on state approval. At the extreme,
              a state could veto federal authority outright by denying or revoking
              a license. Both outcomes are squarely preempted. This conclusion applies
              to any state’s money transmitter licensing regime, including states
              that limit their licensing exemptions to a subset of national banks
              (such as Iowa’s insured-deposits-only carveout).\n\n2. Exclusive Federal
              Visitorial Authority\n\nSeparately, 12 U.S.C. § 484 vests the OCC with
              exclusive visitorial authority over national banks. “No national bank
              shall be subject to any visitorial powers except as authorized by Federal
              law.” Iowa’s money transmitter statute grants the state agency robust
              supervisory jurisdiction over licensees, including the power to demand
              books and records, conduct periodic examinations, take enforcement actions,
              and even place a licensee into receivership. Applying that regime to
              a national bank would be “fundamentally inconsistent” with the OCC’s
              exclusive visitorial powers and is therefore impermissible on independent
              grounds.\n\nTogether, these two bases lead to a clean and sweeping conclusion:
              a national bank may conduct its federally authorized activities in any
              state without a state money transmitter license, regardless of whether
              it qualifies for any state-law exemption.\n\nOur Take\n\nThe OCC’s conclusion
              here was entirely expected. The preemption framework for national banks
              is well-settled, and the OCC’s letter largely restates principles the
              Supreme Court and federal courts have applied for decades. That said,
              one nuance in this letter deserves closer attention: state-chartered
              trust banks are in a very different position.\n\nUnlike national banks,
              state trust companies and state-chartered banks do not benefit from
              National Bank Act preemption. Their ability to avoid state money transmitter
              licensing requirements depends entirely on how each individual state
              defines “bank” or “trust company” in its money transmission statute
              and those definitions vary considerably.\n\nPrint:"}], "support_state":

              that Fidelity Digital Assets, National Association (the recently converted
              national trust bank formerly known as Fidelity Digital Assets Service,
              LLC) is not required to hold state money transmitter licenses to conduct
              its federally authorized activities. The OCC concluded that the National
              Bank Act preempts any state money transmitter licensing requirement
              as applied to a national bank.\n\nUntil December 12, 2025, Fidelity
              Digital Assets operated as a New York-chartered limited liability trust
              company and held money transmitter licenses in numerous states, including
              Iowa. On that date, the OCC approved its conversion to an uninsured
              national trust bank under 12 U.S.C. § 27(a). Concurrent with the conversion,
              the Bank surrendered its Iowa money transmitter license.\n\nIowa pushed
              back. Its money transmitter statute exempts banks and trust companies
              from licensing, but only if they hold federally insured deposits. Because
              Fidelity Digital Assets is an uninsured national bank, Iowa argued the
              exemption did not apply and requested a legal basis for the license
              surrender. Fidelity Digital Assets responded that the National Bank
              Act preempts Iowa’s requirements and asked the OCC to confirm that position.\n\nThe
              OCC’s analysis of whether a state can require a national bank to obtain
              a state money transmitter license as a condition of engaging in federally
              authorized activities, including cryptocurrency custody, trade execution,
              stablecoin issuance, and related digital asset services, rested on two
              independent and well-established pillars of federal banking law:\n\n1.
              National Bank Act Preemption\n\nFederal law authorizes national banks
              to conduct a broad range of activities on a national basis. Any state
              law that “prevents or significantly interferes” with a national bank’s
              exercise of its federally authorized powers is preempted.\n\nThe OCC
              reasoned that requiring a national bank to obtain a state money transmitter
              license, even as a threshold condition to operating, would impermissibly
              condition the Bank’s federal authority on state approval. At the extreme,
              a state could veto federal authority outright by denying or revoking
              a license. Both outcomes are squarely preempted. This conclusion applies
              to any state’s money transmitter licensing regime, including states
              that limit their licensing exemptions to a subset of national banks
              (such as Iowa’s insured-deposits-only carveout).\n\n2. Exclusive Federal
              Visitorial Authority\n\nSeparately, 12 U.S.C. § 484 vests the OCC with
              exclusive visitorial authority over national banks. “No national bank
              shall be subject to any visitorial powers except as authorized by Federal
              law.” Iowa’s money transmitter statute grants the state agency robust
              supervisory jurisdiction over licensees, including the power to demand
              books and records, conduct periodic examinations, take enforcement actions,
              and even place a licensee into receivership. Applying that regime to
              a national bank would be “fundamentally inconsistent” with the OCC’s
              exclusive visitorial powers and is therefore impermissible on independent
              grounds.\n\nTogether, these two bases lead to a clean and sweeping conclusion:
              a national bank may conduct its federally authorized activities in any
              state without a state money transmitter license, regardless of whether
              it qualifies for any state-law exemption.\n\nOur Take\n\nThe OCC’s conclusion
              here was entirely expected. The preemption framework for national banks
              is well-settled, and the OCC’s letter largely restates principles the
              Supreme Court and federal courts have applied for decades. That said,
              one nuance in this letter deserves closer attention: state-chartered
              trust banks are in a very different position.\n\nUnlike national banks,
              state trust companies and state-chartered banks do not benefit from
              National Bank Act preemption. Their ability to avoid state money transmitter
              licensing requirements depends entirely on how each individual state
              defines “bank” or “trust company” in its money transmission statute
              and those definitions vary considerably.\n\nPrint:"}], "research_history":

              {"source_id": "SRC-LOCAL-5b01121f7bfd7357746c", "source_hash": "58b0379461c2b3d9c58807fff3ac3f7136d5aedd4f20022fc8be9eeb64cec409",

              "original_path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/facts.md", "title": "facts.md",
              "support_state": "supplied", "source_type": "workspace", "available_excerpt":
              "# Known Facts\n\n- Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted
              Nov 15 (~10 weeks out).\n- Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k
              business accounts into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with
              one unified account and balance and full access to Mosaic''s product
