              "path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/sources/SRC-LOCAL-843f945d0832ba97e71a.md",
              "original_path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/dossier.md", "title": "dossier.md",
              "support_state": "supplied", "source_type": "workspace", "available_excerpt":
              "# Harbor 2 matter dossier\n\n## Current position\n\nThe Harbor Pay
              migration needs legal and compliance review before the planned Nov 15
              close. This is the accepted working view. No decision has been recorded.\n\nThis
              draft recommends continuing close preparation but making the day-one
              service migration conditional. Mosaic should not give all Harbor users
              full access until:\n\n1. Mosaic has documented authority for each post-close
              service in each affected state.\n2. Compliance confirms that Mosaic
              may rely on Harbor’s know-your-customer (KYC) results, or defines and
              completes remediation.\n3. Authorized reviewers assess Harbor’s open
              alerts and suspicious activity report (SAR) history.\n4. Mosaic tests
              the replacement transaction-monitoring feed and finds no material coverage
              gap.\n\nIf a condition is not met, Mosaic should hold the affected state
              launch, restrict affected accounts, or delay full product access. The
              $50 welcome bonus should also wait for review of its structure, terms,
              funding, and disclosures.\n\nThe saved material does not establish that
              the acquisition close itself must wait. However, the unread alerts and
              SAR history could affect deal terms, risk allocation, or the decision
              to close.\n\n### Assumptions used\n\n- Harbor is subject to the state
              money-transmission and federal anti-money-laundering requirements discussed
              below. The licensing, KYC, alert, and monitoring conclusions depend
              on this unverified legal premise.\n- Mosaic will become the operating
              provider when Harbor users receive a unified Mosaic account, combined
              balance, and access to Mosaic products. The licensing analysis depends
              on this inference.\n- The analysis does not assume that Harbor’s licenses
              transfer, that Harbor’s KYC results satisfy Mosaic’s program, or that
              the monitoring transition will work without a gap.\n\n### Record conflicts\n\n-
              Harbor reportedly has licenses in 38 states, Mosaic has licenses in
              41 states, and the combined footprint is 44 states. A 44-state footprint
              is three states larger than Mosaic’s 41-state footprint, but the record
              says the acquisition opens four new markets. The license lists and the
              intended meaning of “market” are needed. Until then, the states requiring
              separate authority cannot be identified reliably.\n- Matter metadata
              gives a target date of `2026-09-11`. The reported close is “Nov 15,”
              approximately ten weeks after the Sept. 9 intake. A saved hypothetical
              uses November 15, 2026, but that does not establish the actual closing
              year. The operative close date and year remain unresolved.\n\n## Decision
              question\n\nDoes any part of the Harbor Pay acquisition migration need
              legal review before the Nov 15 close?\n\n## Issues\n\n<!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-94e42e2b38090045
              -->\n### Money transmission licensing: whether Mosaic Relay can operate
              under the combined 44-state footprint and whether Harbor''s MTLs transfer/survive
              the acquisition\n\n**Current answer**\n\nMosaic should not treat Harbor’s
              money transmitter licenses as assets that automatically move to Mosaic
              through the reported asset purchase. Mosaic should not start regulated
              services in a state unless it has documented authority for its complete
              post-close activity.\n\nThe acquisition close and the service launch
              can be managed as separate milestones. If authority is not established,
              the present fallback is to hold the affected state launch or restrict
              regulated functions.\n\n**Rule and support**\n\nSaved research concludes
              that the answer must be determined state by state. The review must cover
              Mosaic’s authority, transaction notices or approvals, interim operations,
              outstanding customer obligations, and Harbor’s license surrender.\n\nFour
              sources were retrieved, but no operative passage was selected, read,
              or verified. They do not establish the rule in any affected state:\n\n-
              [Money transmission research packet](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/RES-20260911-0a5f07.md)\n-
              [source:SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538]\n- [source:SRC-71b20ecf65825d6522c4]\n-
              [source:SRC-e6c1e4e85e004ccbe413]\n- [source:SRC-b48d8d40f5a0cfe9a200]\n\nThe
              model act is not proof of any state’s adopted law. The premise that
              an asset purchase does not automatically give Mosaic Harbor’s operating
              authority remains an unverified state-law conclusion.\n\n**Application**\n\nMosaic
              plans to use or assume Harbor’s licenses in the new markets. The planned
              unified Mosaic account, combined balance, and access to Mosaic products
              indicate that Mosaic may become the actual provider. If so, keeping
              Harbor’s entity or licenses active might not authorize Mosaic’s conduct.\n\nHarbor
              could remain the licensed provider during a transition only if customer
              contracts, funds flow, operating control, licenses, bonds, records,
              and applicable state rules support that result. The documents and actual
              operations must match.\n\nA partner bank holding funds would not alone
              resolve the issue. The analysis still depends on who contracts with
              users, controls transfers, owes repayment, records balances, resolves
              errors, and performs regulated duties.\n\n**Next step**\n\nIdentify
              the Harbor-only jurisdictions and prepare a state matrix. For each state,
              determine Mosaic’s authority, required filings or approvals, operation
              while an application is pending, treatment of customer obligations,
              Harbor’s run-off duties, and the launch restriction needed if authority
              is not established.\n\n<!-- retained-issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-94e42e2b38090045:start
              -->\n<details>\n<summary>Saved research and prior analysis</summary>\n\nPreserved
              research snapshot. Its facts and assumptions may predate later records.
              Use the current answer above for application to the current matter.\n\nDo
              not rely on transferability without an applicable state rule, approval,
              or written regulator position.\n\nThe answer must be determined state
              by state and must cover more than technical change-of-control rules.\n\nThis
              path is possible only if Harbor remains the real provider and the relevant
              states permit the arrangement. The unified Mosaic account design may
              conflict with that position.\n\nT", "selected_passages": [{"start":

              "text": "ignment for the benefit of its \ncreditors; or \n(3) \nthe
              commencement of a proceeding to revoke or suspend its \nlicense in a
              state or country in which the licensee engages in business or is licensed.
              \n(b) \nA licensee shall file a report with the [Commissioner] within
              three business \nday after the licensee has reason to know of the occurrence
              of any of the following events: \n(1) \na [charge or] conviction of
              the licensee or of a key individual \nor person in control of the licensee
              for a felony; or \n(2) \na [charge or] conviction of an authorized delegate
              for a \nfelony. \nSection 7.05 Bank Secrecy Act Reports. \nA licensee
              and an authorized delegate shall file all reports required by federal
              currency \nreporting, record keeping, and suspicious activity reporting
              requirements as set forth in the Bank \nSecrecy Act and other federal
              and state laws pertaining to money laundering. The timely filing of
              \na complete and accurate report required under this [Section 7.05]
              with the appropriate federal \nagency is deemed compliant with the requirements
              of this [Section 7.05]. \nSection 7.06 Records. \n(a) \nLicensee shall
              maintain the following records, for determining its \ncompliance with
              this [Act] for at least [three] years: \n(1) \na record of each outstanding
              money transmission obligation \nsold; \n(2) \na general ledger posted

              CSBS Money Transmission Modernization Act", "extraction_state": "complete",
              "selected_passages": [{"unit_id": "p000004", "start": 0, "end": 2200,
              "page_number": 4, "section_label": null, "body_hash": "2245b178c49fc1f157bf15c133c59f8fcfe9abdf43f0bf94df397229a7889584",
              "path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000004.md",
              "text": "4 \n \nJune 30, September 30, and December 31. \n(d) \n\"Bank
              Secrecy Act\" means the Bank Secrecy Act, 31 U.S.C. Section 5311, \net
              seq. and its implementing regulations, as amended and recodified from
              time to time. \n(e) \n\"Closed loop stored value\" means stored value
              that is redeemable by the \nissuer only for goods or services provided
              by the issuer or its affiliate or franchisees of the issuer \nor its
              affiliate, except to the extent required by applicable law to be redeemable
              in cash for its cash \nvalue; \n(f) \n\"Control\" means \n(1) \n(A)
              the power to vote, directly or indirectly, at least 25 percent of \nthe
              outstanding voting shares or voting interests of a licensee or person
              in control of a \nlicensee; \n(B) \nthe power to elect or appoint a
              majority of key individuals or \nexecutive officers, managers, directors,
              trustees, or other persons exercising \nmanagerial authority of a person
              in control of a licensee; or \n(C) \nthe power to exercise, directly
              or indirectly, a controlling \ninfluence over the management or policies
              of a licensee or person in control of a \nlicensee. \n(2) \nRebuttable
              Presumption of Control. \n(A) \nA person is presumed to exercise a controlling
              influence \nwhen the person holds the power to vote, directly or indirectly,
              at least 10 percent \nof the outstanding voting shares or voting interests
              of a licensee or person in control \nof a licensee.2 \n(B) \nA person
              presumed to exercise a controlling influence as \ndefined by this [Section
              2.01(f)] can rebut the presumption of control if the person \nis a passive
              investor. \n(3) \nFor purposes of determining the percentage of a person
              controlled \nby any other person, the person''s interest shall be aggregated
              with the interest of any other \nimmediate family member, including
              the person''s spouse, parents, children, siblings, \nmothers- and fathers-in
              law, sons- and daughters-in-law, brothers- and sisters-in-law, and \nany
              other person who shares such person''s home. \n(g) \n\"Eligible rating\"
              shall mean a credit rating of any of the three highest rating \ncategories
              provided by an eligible rating service, whereby each category may include

              voting shares or voting interests of a licensee or person in control

              "# Issues and workstreams\n\n- Money transmission licensing: whether
              Mosaic Relay can operate under the combined 44-state footprint and whether
              Harbor''s MTLs transfer/survive the acquisition\n- BSA/AML and KYC:
              whether relying on Harbor''s prior KYC (with missing underlying documents
              for pre-2023 users) satisfies Mosaic Relay''s independent CIP/AML obligations\n-
              SAR and alert handling: obligations to review, file, and manage Harbor''s
              ~40 open alerts and SARs, and successor liability\n- Monitoring vendor
              transition: continuity of transaction monitoring when the SaaS contract
              terminates at close\n- Marketing compliance: the $50 welcome bonus offer
              and any state money transmission or consumer protection implications\n-
              Customer account, contract, and data-transfer rights <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-af341445a7af4c06
              -->\n", "selected_passages": [{"start": 0, "end": 817, "text": "# Issues
              and workstreams\n\n- Money transmission licensing: whether Mosaic Relay
              can operate under the combined 44-state footprint and whether Harbor''s
              MTLs transfer/survive the acquisition\n- BSA/AML and KYC: whether relying
              on Harbor''s prior KYC (with missing underlying documents for pre-2023
              users) satisfies Mosaic Relay''s independent CIP/AML obligations\n-
              SAR and alert handling: obligations to review, file, and manage Harbor''s
              ~40 open alerts and SARs, and successor liability\n- Monitoring vendor
              transition: continuity of transaction monitoring when the SaaS contract
              terminates at close\n- Marketing compliance: the $50 welcome bonus offer
              and any state money transmission or consumer protection implications\n-
              Customer account, contract, and data-transfer rights <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-af341445a7af4c06
              -->\n"}], "content_truncated": false, "source_label": "issues.md"},
              {"source_id": "SRC-LOCAL-5b01121f7bfd7357746c", "source_hash": "58b0379461c2b3d9c58807fff3ac3f7136d5aedd4f20022fc8be9eeb64cec409",
              "source_version": "58b0379461c2b3d9c58807fff3ac3f7136d5aedd4f20022fc8be9eeb64cec409",
              "path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/sources/SRC-LOCAL-5b01121f7bfd7357746c.md",
              "original_path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/facts.md", "title": "facts.md",
              "support_state": "supplied", "source_type": "workspace", "available_excerpt":
              "# Known Facts\n\n- Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted
              Nov 15 (~10 weeks out).\n- Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k
              business accounts into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with
              one unified account and balance and full access to Mosaic''s product
              set.\n- Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC''d
              by Harbor.\n- Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states;
              Mosaic Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening four
              new markets.\n- Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in
              2024; Mosaic has pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying
              documents for users onboarded before 2023.\n- Harbor''s transaction
              monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract terminates at close;
              plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction feed at Mosaic''s engine on
              day 1.\n- Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50 bonus on
              first transfer, launching close+1.\n- Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts
              and ''a handful'' of SARs from the last year at Harbor; nobody has read
              them yet.\n- Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts
              into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account
              and balance.\n- Plan is no re-verification of Harbor''s existing KYC;
              Harbor users were already KYC''d.\n- Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor
              that shut down in 2024; pass/fail results exist for everyone but underlying
              documents are missing for users onboarded before 2023.\n- Harbor''s
              transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract terminates
              at close; plan is to repoint the transaction feed to Mosaic Relay''s
              engine on day 1.\n- Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful''
              of SARs from the last year at Harbor; none have been read yet.\n- How
              is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase (Mosaic buys
              Harbor''s assets)\n- Does Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program currently
              permit relying on another institution''s prior KYC without re-verification,
              or is re-verification required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance\n-
              What is known about Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and the SARs from the
              last year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence\n- For the four
              new markets opened by the combined footprint, does Mosaic Relay plan
              to operate under Harbor''s existing licenses or apply for its own? —
              Use/assume Harbor''s licenses\n- For the pre-2023 Harbor users with
              no underlying KYC documents, what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s
              own BSA/AML customer identification and recordkeeping obligations? —
              It is not yet known whether Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program permits
              reliance on Harbor''s prior KYC; compliance must confirm.\n- Have the
              ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last year been reviewed,
              and what did they reveal? — The open alerts and SAR history have not
              been reviewed and remain in diligence.\n- For the four new markets opened
              by the combined license footprint, what is the plan for state money
              transmission licensing or approval before onboarding those customers?
              — Mosaic Relay currently plans to use or assume Harbor''s licenses for
              the four new markets.\n\n## Assumptions\n\n- [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s
              existing money transmission licenses and Harbor''s MTLs are transferable
              or can be maintained through the acquisition without new state approval\n-
              [Assumption] The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy Mosaic
              Relay''s own BSA/AML program obligations without the underlying documents\n-
              [Assumption] The transaction monitoring repoint can be completed and
              validated before close without a monitoring gap\n- [Assumption] Harbor
              Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject to state MTL regimes and
              federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).\n- [Assumption] Mosaic
              Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter in 41 states (per the request).\n-
              [Assumption] The acquisition is structured as an asset or stock purchase,
              which affects whether Harbor''s licenses and SAR/alert obligations transfer
              (structure not yet confirmed).\n", "selected_passages": [{"start": 0,
              "end": 3962, "text": "# Known Facts\n\n- Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor
              Pay; close targeted Nov 15 (~10 weeks out).\n- Migration moves 240k
              consumer users and 12k business accounts into Mosaic Relay''s app on
              day 1 post-close, with one unified account and balance and full access
              to Mosaic''s product set.\n- Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users
              were already KYC''d by Harbor.\n- Harbor holds money transmitter licenses
              (MTLs) in 38 states; Mosaic Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44
              states, opening four new markets.\n- Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor
              that shut down in 2024; Mosaic has pass/fail results for everyone but
              not the underlying documents for users onboarded before 2023.\n- Harbor''s
              transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract terminates
              at close; plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction feed at Mosaic''s
              engine on day 1.\n- Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50
              bonus on first transfer, launching close+1.\n- Diligence flagged ~40
              open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from the last year at Harbor;
              nobody has read them yet.\n- Migration moves 240k consumer users and
              12k business accounts into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close,
              with one unified account and balance.\n- Plan is no re-verification
              of Harbor''s existing KYC; Harbor users were already KYC''d.\n- Harbor''s
              KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail results exist
              for everyone but underlying documents are missing for users onboarded
              before 2023.\n- Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS
              whose contract terminates at close; plan is to repoint the transaction
              feed to Mosaic Relay''s engine on day 1.\n- Diligence flagged ~40 open
              alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from the last year at Harbor; none
              have been read yet.\n- How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured?
              — Asset purchase (Mosaic buys Harbor''s assets)\n- Does Mosaic Relay''s
              AML/CIP program currently permit relying on another institution''s prior
              KYC without re-verification, or is re-verification required? — Not sure
              / need to check with compliance\n- What is known about Harbor''s ~40
              open alerts and the SARs from the last year? — Nothing reviewed yet
              — still in diligence\n- For the four new markets opened by the combined
              footprint, does Mosaic Relay plan to operate under Harbor''s existing
              licenses or apply for its own? — Use/assume Harbor''s licenses\n- For
              the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents, what is
              the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML customer identification
              and recordkeeping obligations? — It is not yet known whether Mosaic
              Relay''s AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor''s prior KYC; compliance
              must confirm.\n- Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from
              the last year been reviewed, and what did they reveal? — The open alerts
              and SAR history have not been reviewed and remain in diligence.\n- For
              the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint, what
              is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval before
              onboarding those customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans to use or
              assume Harbor''s licenses for the four new markets.\n\n## Assumptions\n\n-
              [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s existing money transmission licenses and
              Harbor''s MTLs are transferable or can be maintained through the acquisition
              without new state approval\n- [Assumption] The KYC pass/fail results
              are sufficient to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML program obligations
              without the underlying documents\n- [Assumption] The transaction monitoring
              repoint can be completed and validated before close without a monitoring
              gap\n- [Assumption] Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject
              to state MTL regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).\n-
              [Assumption] Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter in
              41 states (per the request).\n- [Assumption] The acquisition is structured
              as an asset or stock purchase, which affects whether Harbor''s licenses
              and SAR/alert obligations transfer (structure not yet confirmed).\n"}],

              CSBS Money Transmission Modernization Act", "extraction_state": "complete",

              "page_number": 27, "section_label": null, "body_hash": "512d4a7a3e1afc61a66c79b53548e6795e9f434d557b21d346fd4662aaafc705",
              "path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000027.md",
              "text": "27 \n \n(c) \nThe audited financial statements shall include
              or be accompanied by a \ncertificate of opinion of the independent certified
              public accountant or independent public \naccountant that is satisfactory
              in form and content to the [Commissioner]. If the certificate or \nopinion
              is qualified, the [Commissioner] may order the licensee to take any
              action as the \n[Commissioner] may find necessary to enable the independent
              or certified public accountant or \nindependent public accountant to
              remove the qualification. \nSection 7.03 Authorized Delegate Reporting.
              \n(a) \nEach licensee shall submit a report of authorized delegates
              within 45 days \nof the end of the calendar quarter.20 The [Commissioner]
              is authorized and encouraged to utilize \nNMLS for the submission of
              the report required by this [Section 7.03(a)] provided that such \nfunctionality
              is consistent with the requirements of this [Section 7.03]. \n(b) \nThe
              authorized delegate report shall include, at a minimum, each authorized
              \ndelegate''s: \n(1) \nCompany legal name; \n(2) \nTaxpayer employer
              identification number; \n(3) \nPrincipal provider identifier; \n(4)
              \nPhysical address; \n(5) \nMailing address; \n(6) \nAny business conducted
              in other states; \n(7) \nAny fictitious or trade name; \n(8) \nContact
              person name, phone number, and email \n(9) \nStart date as licensee’s
              authorized delegate; \n(10) \nEnd date acting as licensee’s authorized
              delegate, if applicable;  \n(11) \n[Court orders pursuant to [Section

              "original_path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/sources/RUN-20260911-d08e84-37ee676da5b354ba8538-fetch.md.bin",
              "path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000027.md",
              "source_hash": "512d4a7a3e1afc61a66c79b53548e6795e9f434d557b21d346fd4662aaafc705",
              "source_label": "[PDF] CSBS Money Transmission Modernization Act — Page
              27, characters 0–1943", "unit_id": "p000027", "locator": "Page 27, characters
              0–1943", "available_excerpt": "27 \n \n(c) \nThe audited financial statements
              shall include or be accompanied by a \ncertificate of opinion of the
              independent certified public accountant or independent public \naccountant
              that is satisfactory in form and content to the [Commissioner]. If the
              certificate or \nopinion is qualified, the [Commissioner] may order
              the licensee to take any action as the \n[Commissioner] may find necessary
              to enable the independent or certified public accountant or \nindependent
              public accountant to remove the qualification. \nSection 7.03 Authorized
              Delegate Reporting. \n(a) \nEach licensee shall submit a report of authorized
              delegates within 45 days \nof the end of the calendar quarter.20 The
              [Commissioner] is authorized and encouraged to utilize \nNMLS for the
              submission of the report required by this [Section 7.03(a)] provided
              that such \nfunctionality is consistent with the requirements of this
              [Section 7.03]. \n(b) \nThe authorized delegate report shall include,
              at a minimum, each authorized \ndelegate''s: \n(1) \nCompany legal name;
              \n(2) \nTaxpayer employer identification number; \n(3) \nPrincipal provider
              identifier; \n(4) \nPhysical address; \n(5) \nMailing address; \n(6)
              \nAny business conducted in other states; \n(7) \nAny fictitious or
              trade name; \n(8) \nContact person name, phone number, and email \n(9)
              \nStart date as licensee’s authorized delegate; \n(10) \nEnd date acting
              as licensee’s authorized delegate, if applicable;  \n(11) \n[Court orders
              pursuant to [Section 8.03];] and \n(12) \nAny other information the
              [Commissioner] reasonably requires with \nrespect to the authorized
              delegate. \nSection 7.04 Reports of Certain Events.21 \n \n20 Commentary:
              This language is designed to implement state use of the NMLS Uniform
              Authorized Agent Reporting \n(UAAR) process. \n21 Commentary: States
              are encouraged to utilize NMLS to satisfy Section 7.04 reporting requirements
              if NMLS \ndevelops new functionality to prioritize reporting of significant
              events.\n"}, {"source_id": "SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538", "source_version":
              "dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a", "title": "[PDF] CSBS Money Transmission
              Modernization Act", "extraction_state": "complete", "selected_passages":
              [{"unit_id": "p000028", "start": 0, "end": 2132, "page_number": 28,
              "section_label": null, "body_hash": "80c098d06593529d6d6335e3b8a4fe8e8db356a8c5d82eb34a2001d27d642973",
              "path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000028.md",
              "text": "28 \n \n(a) \nA licensee shall file a report with the [Commissioner]
              within one business \nday after the licensee has reason to know of the
              occurrence of any of the following events: \n(1) \nthe filing of a petition
              by or against the licensee under the \nUnited States Bankruptcy Code,
              11 U.S.C. Section 101-110, as amended or recodified from \ntime to time,
              for bankruptcy or reorganization; \n(2) \nthe filing of a petition by
              or against the licensee for \nreceivership, the commencement of any
              other judicial or administrative proceeding for its \ndissolution or
              reorganization, or the making of a general assignment for the benefit
              of its \ncreditors; or \n(3) \nthe commencement of a proceeding to revoke
              or suspend its \nlicense in a state or country in which the licensee
              engages in business or is licensed. \n(b) \nA licensee shall file a
              report with the [Commissioner] within three business \nday after the
              licensee has reason to know of the occurrence of any of the following
              events: \n(1) \na [charge or] conviction of the licensee or of a key
              individual \nor person in control of the licensee for a felony; or \n(2)
              \na [charge or] conviction of an authorized delegate for a \nfelony.
              \nSection 7.05 Bank Secrecy Act Reports. \nA licensee and an authorized
              delegate shall file all reports required by federal currency \nreporting,
              record keeping, and suspicious activity reporting requirements as set
              forth in the Bank \nSecrecy Act and other federal and state laws pertaining
              to money laundering. The timely filing of \na complete and accurate
              report required under this [Section 7.05] with the appropriate federal
              \nagency is deemed compliant with the requirements of this [Section
              7.05]. \nSection 7.06 Records. \n(a) \nLicensee shall maintain the following
              records, for determining its \ncompliance with this [Act] for at least
              [three] years: \n(1) \na record of each outstanding money transmission
              obligation \nsold; \n(2) \na general ledger posted at least monthly
              containing all asset, \nliability, capital, income, and expense accounts;
              \n(3) \nbank statements and bank reconciliation records; \n(4) \nrecords
              of outstanding money transmission obligations;\n"}], "support_state":

              "text": "29 \n \n(5) \nrecords of each outstanding money transmission
              obligation \npaid within the [three]-year period; \n(6) \na list of
              the last known names and addresses of all of the \nlicensee''s authorized
              delegates; and \n(7) \nany other records the [Commissioner] reasonably
              requires \nby rule. \n(b) \nThe items specified in [Section 7.06(a)]
              may be maintained in any form of \nrecord. \n(c) \nRecords specified
              in [Section 7.06(a)] may be maintained outside this state \nif they
              are made accessible to the [Commissioner] on [seven] business-days''
              notice that is sent in \na record. \n(d) \nAll records maintained by
              the licensee as required in [Section 7.06(a)–(c)] \nare open to inspection
              by the [Commissioner] pursuant to [Section 4.03(a)]. \n \nARTICLE VIII
              \nAuthorized Delegates \nSection 8.01 Relationship Between Licensee
              and Authorized Delegate. \n(a) \nIn this [Section 8.01], \"remit\" means
              to make direct payments of money to \na licensee or its representative
              authorized to receive money or to deposit money in a bank in an \naccount
              specified by the licensee. \n(b) \nBefore a licensee is authorized to
              conduct business through an authorized \ndelegate or allows a person
              to act as the licensee''s authorized delegate, the licensee must: \n(1)
              \nadopt, and update as necessary, written policies and procedures \nreasonably
              designed to ensure that the licensee''s authorized delegates comply
              with \napplicable state and federal law; \n(2) \nenter into a written
              contract that complies with [Section 8.01(d)]; \nand \n(3) \nconduct
              a reasonable risk-based background investigation sufficient \nfor the
              licensee to determine whether the authorized delegate has complied and
              will likely \ncomply with applicable state and federal law. \n(c) \nAn
              authorized delegate must operate in full compliance with this [Act].
              \n(d) \nThe written contract required by [Section 8.01(b)] must be signed
              by the \nlicensee and the authorized delegate and, at a minimum, must:\n"}],

              "text": "12 \n \n(4) \nThe terms of or a copy of any bond filed by a

              and \n(e) \nImposition of an administrative fine or penalty under this
              [Act]. \nSection 4.03 Supervision. \n(a) \nThe [Commissioner] may conduct
              an examination or investigation of a \nlicensee or authorized delegate
              or otherwise take independent action authorized by this [Act] or by
              \na rule adopted or order issued under this [Act] as reasonably necessary
              or appropriate to administer \nand enforce this [Act], regulations implementing
              this [Act], and other applicable law, including \nthe Bank Secrecy Act
              and the USA PATRIOT ACT.  The [Commissioner] may: \n(1) \nconduct an
              examination either on-site or off-site as the \n[Commissioner] may reasonably
              require; \n(2) \nconduct an examination in conjunction with an examination
              \nconducted by representatives of other state agencies or agencies of
              another state or of the \nfederal government; \n(3) \n  accept the examination
              report of another state agency or an agency \nof another state or of
              the federal government, or a report prepared by an independent \naccounting
              firm, which on being accepted is considered for all purposes as an official
              report \nof the [Commissioner]; and \n(4) \nsummon and examine under
              oath a key individual or employee of a \nlicensee or authorized delegate
              and require the person to produce records regarding any \nmatter related
              to the condition and business of the licensee or authorized delegate.
              \n(b) \nA licensee or authorized delegate shall provide, and the [Commissioner]
              \nshall have full and complete access to, all records the [Commissioner]
              may reasonably require to \nconduct a complete examination. The records
              must be provided at the location and in the format \nspecified by the
              [Commissioner], provided, the [Commissioner] may utilize multistate
              record \nproduction standards and examination procedures when such standards
              will reasonably achieve \nthe requirements of this [Section 4.03(b)].8
              \n(c) \nUnless otherwise directed by the [Commissioner], a licensee
              shall pay all \ncosts reasonably incurred in connection with an examination
              of the licensee or the licensee''s \n \n8 Commentary: The [Commissioner]
              is encouraged to instruct examiners to: (1) include all examination
              requests in \nthe Day 1 letter that may require the licensee to obtain
              records located outside of the U.S., including but not limited \nto
              evidence demonstrating when an outstanding money transmission obligation
              has been extinguished; and (2) accept \nelectronic bank statements as
              provided to the licensee by the bank.\n"}], "support_state": "retrieved",

              "original_path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/issues.md", "title": "issues.md",
              "support_state": "supplied", "source_type": "workspace", "available_excerpt":
              "# Issues and workstreams\n\n- Money transmission licensing: whether
              Mosaic Relay can operate under the combined 44-state footprint and whether
              Harbor''s MTLs transfer/survive the acquisition\n- BSA/AML and KYC:
              whether relying on Harbor''s prior KYC (with missing underlying documents

              {"source_id": "SRC-LOCAL-5b01121f7bfd7357746c", "source_hash": "58b0379461c2b3d9c58807fff3ac3f7136d5aedd4f20022fc8be9eeb64cec409",

              "path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/sources/SRC-LOCAL-5b01121f7bfd7357746c.md",
              "original_path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/facts.md", "title": "facts.md",
              "support_state": "supplied", "source_type": "workspace", "available_excerpt":
              "# Known Facts\n\n- Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted
              Nov 15 (~10 weeks out).\n- Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k
              business accounts into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with
              one unified account and balance and full access to Mosaic''s product
              set.\n- Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC''d
              by Harbor.\n- Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states;
              Mosaic Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening four
              new markets.\n- Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in
              2024; Mosaic has pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying
              documents for users onboarded before 2023.\n- Harbor''s transaction
              monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract terminates at close;
              plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction feed at Mosaic''s engine on
              day 1.\n- Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50 bonus on
              first transfer, launching close+1.\n- Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts
              and ''a handful'' of SARs from the last year at Harbor; nobody has read
              them yet.\n- Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts
              into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account
              and balance.\n- Plan is no re-verification of Harbor''s existing KYC;
              Harbor users were already KYC''d.\n- Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor
              that shut down in 2024; pass/fail results exist for everyone but underlying
              documents are missing for users onboarded before 2023.\n- Harbor''s
              transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract terminates
              at close; plan is to repoint the transaction feed to Mosaic Relay''s
              engine on day 1.\n- Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful''
              of SARs from the last year at Harbor; none have been read yet.\n- How
              is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase (Mosaic buys
              Harbor''s assets)\n- Does Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program currently
              permit relying on another institution''s prior KYC without re-verification,
              or is re-verification required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance\n-
              What is known about Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and the SARs from the
              last year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence\n- For the four
              new markets opened by the combined footprint, does Mosaic Relay plan
              to operate under Harbor''s existing licenses or apply for its own? —
              Use/assume Harbor''s licenses\n- For the pre-2023 Harbor users with
              no underlying KYC documents, what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s
              own BSA/AML customer identification and recordkeeping obligations? —
              It is not yet known whether Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program permits
              reliance on Harbor''s prior KYC; compliance must confirm.\n- Have the
              ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last year been reviewed,
              and what did they reveal? — The open alerts and SAR history have not
              been reviewed and remain in diligence.\n- For the four new markets opened
              by the combined license footprint, what is the plan for state money
              transmission licensing or approval before onboarding those customers?
              — Mosaic Relay currently plans to use or assume Harbor''s licenses for
              the four new markets.\n\n## Assumptions\n\n- [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s
              existing money transmission licenses and Harbor''s MTLs are transferable
              or can be maintained through the acquisition without new state approval\n-
              [Assumption] The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy Mosaic
              Relay''s own BSA/AML program obligations without the underlying documents\n-
              [Assumption] The transaction monitoring repoint can be completed and
              validated before close without a monitoring gap\n- [Assumption] Harbor
              Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject to state MTL regimes and
              federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).\n- [Assumption] Mosaic
              Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter in 41 states (per the request).\n-
              [Assumption] The acquisition is structured as an asset or stock purchase,
              which affects whether Harbor''s licenses and SAR/alert obligations transfer
              (structure not yet confirmed).\n", "selected_passages": [{"start": 0,

              KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail results exist
              for everyone but underlying documents are missing for users onboarded
              before 2023.\n- Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS
              whose contract terminates at close; plan is to repoint the transaction
              feed to Mosaic Relay''s engine on day 1.\n- Diligence flagged ~40 open
              alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from the last year at Harbor; none

              — Asset purchase (Mosaic buys Harbor''s assets)\n- Does Mosaic Relay''s

              / need to check with compliance\n- What is known about Harbor''s ~40
              open alerts and the SARs from the last year? — Nothing reviewed yet
              — still in diligence\n- For the four new markets opened by the combined
              footprint, does Mosaic Relay plan to operate under Harbor''s existing

              the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents, what is

              must confirm.\n- Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from
              the last year been reviewed, and what did they reveal? — The open alerts
              and SAR history have not been reviewed and remain in diligence.\n- For
              the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint, what
              is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval before
              onboarding those customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans to use or
              assume Harbor''s licenses for the four new markets.\n\n## Assumptions\n\n-
              [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s existing money transmission licenses and
              Harbor''s MTLs are transferable or can be maintained through the acquisition
              without new state approval\n- [Assumption] The KYC pass/fail results
              are sufficient to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML program obligations
              without the underlying documents\n- [Assumption] The transaction monitoring
              repoint can be completed and validated before close without a monitoring
              gap\n- [Assumption] Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject
              to state MTL regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).\n-
              [Assumption] Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter in
              41 states (per the request).\n- [Assumption] The acquisition is structured
              as an asset or stock purchase, which affects whether Harbor''s licenses
              and SAR/alert obligations transfer (structure not yet confirmed).\n"}],

              CSBS Money Transmission Modernization Act", "extraction_state": "complete",
              "selected_passages": [{"unit_id": "p000027", "start": 0, "end": 1943,
              "page_number": 27, "section_label": null, "body_hash": "512d4a7a3e1afc61a66c79b53548e6795e9f434d557b21d346fd4662aaafc705",
              "path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000027.md",
              "text": "27 \n \n(c) \nThe audited financial statements shall include
              or be accompanied by a \ncertificate of opinion of the independent certified
              public accountant or independent public \naccountant that is satisfactory
              in form and content to the [Commissioner]. If the certificate or \nopinion
              is qualified, the [Commissioner] may order the licensee to take any
              action as the \n[Commissioner] may find necessary to enable the independent
              or certified public accountant or \nindependent public accountant to
              remove the qualification. \nSection 7.03 Authorized Delegate Reporting.
              \n(a) \nEach licensee shall submit a report of authorized delegates
              within 45 days \nof the end of the calendar quarter.20 The [Commissioner]
              is authorized and encouraged to utilize \nNMLS for the submission of
              the report required by this [Section 7.03(a)] provided that such \nfunctionality
              is consistent with the requirements of this [Section 7.03]. \n(b) \nThe
              authorized delegate report shall include, at a minimum, each authorized
              \ndelegate''s: \n(1) \nCompany legal name; \n(2) \nTaxpayer employer
              identification number; \n(3) \nPrincipal provider identifier; \n(4)
              \nPhysical address; \n(5) \nMailing address; \n(6) \nAny business conducted
              in other states; \n(7) \nAny fictitious or trade name; \n(8) \nContact
              person name, phone number, and email \n(9) \nStart date as licensee’s
              authorized delegate; \n(10) \nEnd date acting as licensee’s authorized
              delegate, if applicable;  \n(11) \n[Court orders pursuant to [Section
              8.03];] and \n(12) \nAny other information the [Commissioner] reasonably
              requires with \nrespect to the authorized delegate. \nSection 7.04 Reports
              of Certain Events.21 \n \n20 Commentary: This language is designed to
              implement state use of the NMLS Uniform Authorized Agent Reporting \n(UAAR)
              process. \n21 Commentary: States are encouraged to utilize NMLS to satisfy
              Section 7.04 reporting requirements if NMLS \ndevelops new functionality
              to prioritize reporting of significant events.\n"}], "support_state":

              Modernization Act", "extraction_state": "complete", "selected_passages":
              [{"unit_id": "p000028", "start": 0, "end": 2132, "page_number": 28,
              "section_label": null, "body_hash": "80c098d06593529d6d6335e3b8a4fe8e8db356a8c5d82eb34a2001d27d642973",
              "path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000028.md",
              "text": "28 \n \n(a) \nA licensee shall file a report with the [Commissioner]
              within one business \nday after the licensee has reason to know of the
              occurrence of any of the following events: \n(1) \nthe filing of a petition
              by or against the licensee under the \nUnited States Bankruptcy Code,
              11 U.S.C. Section 101-110, as amended or recodified from \ntime to time,
              for bankruptcy or reorganization; \n(2) \nthe filing of a petition by
              or against the licensee for \nreceivership, the commencement of any
              other judicial or administrative proceeding for its \ndissolution or
              reorganization, or the making of a general assignment for the benefit
              of its \ncreditors; or \n(3) \nthe commencement of a proceeding to revoke
              or suspend its \nlicense in a state or country in which the licensee
              engages in business or is licensed. \n(b) \nA licensee shall file a
              report with the [Commissioner] within three business \nday after the
              licensee has reason to know of the occurrence of any of the following
              events: \n(1) \na [charge or] conviction of the licensee or of a key
              individual \nor person in control of the licensee for a felony; or \n(2)
              \na [charge or] conviction of an authorized delegate for a \nfelony.
              \nSection 7.05 Bank Secrecy Act Reports. \nA licensee and an authorized
              delegate shall file all reports required by federal currency \nreporting,
              record keeping, and suspicious activity reporting requirements as set
              forth in the Bank \nSecrecy Act and other federal and state laws pertaining
              to money laundering. The timely filing of \na complete and accurate
              report required under this [Section 7.05] with the appropriate federal
              \nagency is deemed compliant with the requirements of this [Section
              7.05]. \nSection 7.06 Records. \n(a) \nLicensee shall maintain the following
              records, for determining its \ncompliance with this [Act] for at least
              [three] years: \n(1) \na record of each outstanding money transmission
              obligation \nsold; \n(2) \na general ledger posted at least monthly
              containing all asset, \nliability, capital, income, and expense accounts;
              \n(3) \nbank statements and bank reconciliation records; \n(4) \nrecords
              of outstanding money transmission obligations;\n"}], "support_state":

              "text": "29 \n \n(5) \nrecords of each outstanding money transmission
              obligation \npaid within the [three]-year period; \n(6) \na list of
              the last known names and addresses of all of the \nlicensee''s authorized
              delegates; and \n(7) \nany other records the [Commissioner] reasonably
              requires \nby rule. \n(b) \nThe items specified in [Section 7.06(a)]
              may be maintained in any form of \nrecord. \n(c) \nRecords specified
              in [Section 7.06(a)] may be maintained outside this state \nif they
              are made accessible to the [Commissioner] on [seven] business-days''
              notice that is sent in \na record. \n(d) \nAll records maintained by
              the licensee as required in [Section 7.06(a)–(c)] \nare open to inspection
              by the [Commissioner] pursuant to [Section 4.03(a)]. \n \nARTICLE VIII
              \nAuthorized Delegates \nSection 8.01 Relationship Between Licensee
              and Authorized Delegate. \n(a) \nIn this [Section 8.01], \"remit\" means
              to make direct payments of money to \na licensee or its representative
              authorized to receive money or to deposit money in a bank in an \naccount
              specified by the licensee. \n(b) \nBefore a licensee is authorized to
              conduct business through an authorized \ndelegate or allows a person
              to act as the licensee''s authorized delegate, the licensee must: \n(1)
              \nadopt, and update as necessary, written policies and procedures \nreasonably
              designed to ensure that the licensee''s authorized delegates comply
              with \napplicable state and federal law; \n(2) \nenter into a written
              contract that complies with [Section 8.01(d)]; \nand \n(3) \nconduct
              a reasonable risk-based background investigation sufficient \nfor the
              licensee to determine whether the authorized delegate has complied and
              will likely \ncomply with applicable state and federal law. \n(c) \nAn
              authorized delegate must operate in full compliance with this [Act].
              \n(d) \nThe written contract required by [Section 8.01(b)] must be signed
              by the \nlicensee and the authorized delegate and, at a minimum, must:\n"}],

    "content": "## Working position\n\nThe Harbor Pay migration needs legal and compliance
    review before the planned close. The leading concern is that an asset purchase
    generally requires Mosaic Relay to confirm its own authority to operate in each
    state; the current plan to use or assume Harbor''s licenses is not established
    as legally effective.\n\nThe second concern is BSA/AML readiness. Mosaic Relay
    has not confirmed whether its AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor''s prior
    KYC, and underlying records are missing for some pre-2023 users. Harbor''s open
    alerts and SAR history also remain unread. These gaps make a day-one migration
    without re-verification or account restrictions difficult to support.\n\nTransaction
    monitoring continuity is also material because Harbor''s vendor ends at close.
    The repointed feed should be tested and validated before migrated users receive
    full access. The $50 bonus is lower priority but still needs review once its eligibility,
    funding, terms, and disclosures are known.\n\n## Plausible alternatives\n\nA narrower
    launch could exclude the four new markets, restrict users whose KYC evidence is
    incomplete, or delay full product access until alert review and monitoring validation
    finish. A full day-one launch remains possible only if state licensing, AML/CIP
    reliance, alert handling, and monitoring continuity are confirmed.\n\n## Material
    facts and assumptions\n\nReported facts include the asset-purchase structure,
    the current plan to rely on Harbor''s licenses, the lack of a compliance answer
    on KYC reliance, and the unread alerts and SAR history. The analysis assumes both
    entities conduct regulated money-transmission activity and that Mosaic Relay will
    become the operating provider immediately after close. It does not assume that
    Harbor''s licenses transfer or that Harbor''s KYC is sufficient.\n\n## What could
    change this view\n\nThe view could change if state counsel confirms an effective
    licensing path for each affected state, compliance confirms permissible reliance
    with adequate records or remediation, diligence clears the alerts and SAR history,
    and testing shows no monitoring gap. The bonus structure remains unknown.\n\n##
    Support limit\n\nThis is generated analysis based on reported matter facts. No

    "number": 2, "content": "### Saved overall view\n\nThe Harbor Pay migration needs

    migration without re-verification or account restrictions difficult to support.\n\nTransaction

    — 1 sources retrieved; 1 with passages read.\n\n<details>\n<summary>Earlier saved
    position — 2026-09-09T20:57:53+00:00</summary>\n\n**Working position**\n\nThe
    Harbor Pay migration needs legal and compliance review before the planned close.
    The leading concern is that an asset purchase generally requires Mosaic Relay
    to confirm its own authority to operate in each state; the current plan to use
    or assume Harbor''s licenses is not established as legally effective.\n\nThe second
    concern is BSA/AML readiness. Mosaic Relay has not confirmed whether its AML/CIP
    program permits reliance on Harbor''s prior KYC, and underlying records are missing
    for some pre-2023 users. Harbor''s open alerts and SAR history also remain unread.
    These gaps make a day-one migration without re-verification or account restrictions
    difficult to support.\n\nTransaction monitoring continuity is also material because
    Harbor''s vendor ends at close. The repointed feed should be tested and validated
    before migrated users receive full access. The $50 bonus is lower priority but
    still needs review once its eligibility, funding, terms, and disclosures are known.\n\n**Plausible
    alternatives**\n\nA narrower launch could exclude the four new markets, restrict
    users whose KYC evidence is incomplete, or delay full product access until alert
    review and monitoring validation finish. A full day-one launch remains possible
    only if state licensing, AML/CIP reliance, alert handling, and monitoring continuity
    are confirmed.\n\n**Material facts and assumptions**\n\nReported facts include
    the asset-purchase structure, the current plan to rely on Harbor''s licenses,
    the lack of a compliance answer on KYC reliance, and the unread alerts and SAR
    history. The analysis assumes both entities conduct regulated money-transmission
    activity and that Mosaic Relay will become the operating provider immediately
    after close. It does not assume that Harbor''s licenses transfer or that Harbor''s
    KYC is sufficient.\n\n**What could change this view**\n\nThe view could change
    if state counsel confirms an effective licensing path for each affected state,
    compliance confirms permissible reliance with adequate records or remediation,
    diligence clears the alerts and SAR history, and testing shows no monitoring gap.

    "text": "14 \n \nARTICLE V \nMoney Transmission Licenses \nSection 5.01 License
    Required. \n(a) \nA person may not engage in the business of money transmission
    or \nadvertise, solicit, or hold itself out as providing money transmission unless
    the person is licensed \nunder this [Act]; \n(b) \n[Section 5.01(a)] does not
    apply to: \n(1) \nA person that is an authorized delegate of a person licensed
    under \nthis [Act] acting within the scope of authority conferred by a written
    contract with the \nlicensee; or \n(2) \nA person that is exempt pursuant to [Section
    3.01] and does not \nengage in money transmission outside the scope of such exemption.
    \n(c) \nA license issued under [Section 5.05] is not transferable or assignable.
    \nSection 5.02 Consistent State Licensing. \n(a) \nTo establish consistent licensing
    between [this state] and other states, the \n[Commissioner] is authorized and
    encouraged to: \n(1) \nimplement all licensing provisions of this [Act] in a manner
    that is \nconsistent with other states that have adopted this [Act]or multistate
    licensing processes; \nand \n(2) \nparticipate in nationwide protocols for licensing
    cooperation and \ncoordination among state regulators provided that such protocols
    are consistent with this \n[Act]. \n(b) \nIn order to fulfill the purposes of
    this [Act], the [Commissioner] is \nauthorized and encouraged to establish relationships
    or contracts with NMLS or other entities \ndesignated by NMLS to enable the [Commissioner]
    to: \n(1) \ncollect and maintain records; \n(2) \ncoordinate multistate licensing
    processes and supervision processes; \n(3) \nprocess fees; and \n(4) \nfacilitate
    communication between [state] and licensees or other \npersons subject to this
    [Act]. \n(c) \nThe [Commissioner] is authorized and encouraged to utilize NMLS
    for all \naspects of licensing in accordance with this [Act], including but not
    limited to, license applications, \napplications for acquisitions of control,
    surety bonds, reporting, criminal history background\n"}], "support_state": "retrieved",

    processes; \nand \n(2) \nparticipate in nationwide protocols for licensing cooperation
    and \ncoordination among state regulators provided that such protocols are consistent
    with this \n[Act]. \n(b) \nIn order to fulfill the purposes of this [Act], the
    [Commissioner] is \nauthorized and encouraged to establish relationships or contracts
    with NMLS or other entities \ndesignated by NMLS to enable the [Commissioner]
    to: \n(1) \ncollect and maintain records; \n(2) \ncoordinate multistate licensing
    processes and supervision processes; \n(3) \nprocess fees; and \n(4) \nfacilitate
    communication between [state] and licensees or other \npersons subject to this
    [Act]. \n(c) \nThe [Commissioner] is authorized and encouraged to utilize NMLS
    for all \naspects of licensing in accordance with this [Act], including but not
    limited to, license applications, \napplications for acquisitions of control,
    surety bonds, reporting, criminal history background\n"}, {"source_id": "SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538",
    "source_version": "dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a", "title": "[PDF] CSBS Money
    Transmission Modernization Act", "extraction_state": "complete", "selected_passages":
    [{"unit_id": "p000021", "start": 0, "end": 2389, "page_number": 21, "section_label":
    null, "body_hash": "5638ae03ab2c6c110a80e30639b8ccd42a1c585fdc2818a38e4f2f0fc69a5e06",
    "path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000021.md",
    "text": "21 \n \nin a medium prescribed by the [Commissioner]. The renewal report
    must state or contain a \ndescription of each material change in information submitted
    by the licensee in its original license \napplication which has not been reported
    to the [Commissioner]. \n(c) \nThe [Commissioner] for good cause may grant an
    extension of the renewal \ndate. \n(d) \nThe [Commissioner] is authorized and
    encouraged to utilize NMLS to \nprocess license renewals provided that such functionality
    is consistent with this [Section 5.06]. \nSection 5.07 Maintenance of License.
    \n(a) \nIf a licensee does not continue to meet the qualifications or satisfy
    the \nrequirements that apply to an applicant for a new money transmission license,
    the [Commissioner] \nmay suspend or revoke the licensee''s license in accordance
    with the procedures established by this \n[Act] or other applicable state law
    for such suspension or revocation. \n(b) \nAn applicant for a money transmission
    license must demonstrate that it \nmeets or will meet, and a money transmission
    licensee must at all times meet, the requirements in \n[Sections 10.01, 10.02,
    and 10.03] of this [Act]. \nARTICLE VI \nAcquisition of Control and Change of
    Key Individual \nSection 6.01 Acquisition of Control. \n(a) \nAny person, or group
    of persons acting in concert, seeking to acquire control \nof a licensee shall
    obtain the written approval of the [Commissioner] prior to acquiring control.
    \nAn individual is not deemed to acquire control of a licensee and is not subject
    to these acquisition \nof control provisions when that individual becomes a key
    individual in the ordinary course of \nbusiness. \n(b) \nA person, or group of
    persons acting in concert, seeking to acquire control \nof a licensee shall, in
    cooperation with the licensee: \n(1) \nSubmit an application in a form and in
    a medium prescribed by the \n[Commissioner]; and \n(2) \nSubmit a nonrefundable
    fee of [$X] with the request for approval. \n(c) \nUpon request, the [Commissioner]
    may permit a licensee or the person, or \ngroup of persons acting in concert,
    to submit some or all information required by the \n[Commissioner] pursuant to
    [Section 6.01(b)(1)] without using NMLS. \n(d) \nThe application required by [Section
    6.01(b)(1)] shall include information \nrequired by [Section 5.04] for any new
    key individuals that have not previously completed the \nrequirements of [Section
    5.04] for a licensee.\n"}], "support_state": "retrieved", "url": "https://www.csbs.org/sites/default/files/2023-02/CSBS%20Money%20Transmission%20Modernization%20Act.pdf",

    "21 \n \nin a medium prescribed by the [Commissioner]. The renewal report must

    is consistent with this [Section 5.06]. \nSection 5.07 Maintenance of License.
    \n(a) \nIf a licensee does not continue to meet the qualifications or satisfy

    license must demonstrate that it \nmeets or will meet, and a money transmission
    licensee must at all times meet, the requirements in \n[Sections 10.01, 10.02,
    and 10.03] of this [Act]. \nARTICLE VI \nAcquisition of Control and Change of
    Key Individual \nSection 6.01 Acquisition of Control. \n(a) \nAny person, or group
    of persons acting in concert, seeking to acquire control \nof a licensee shall
    obtain the written approval of the [Commissioner] prior to acquiring control.
    \nAn individual is not deemed to acquire control of a licensee and is not subject
    to these acquisition \nof control provisions when that individual becomes a key
    individual in the ordinary course of \nbusiness. \n(b) \nA person, or group of
    persons acting in concert, seeking to acquire control \nof a licensee shall, in
    cooperation with the licensee: \n(1) \nSubmit an application in a form and in
    a medium prescribed by the \n[Commissioner]; and \n(2) \nSubmit a nonrefundable
    fee of [$X] with the request for approval. \n(c) \nUpon request, the [Commissioner]
    may permit a licensee or the person, or \ngroup of persons acting in concert,
    to submit some or all information required by the \n[Commissioner] pursuant to
    [Section 6.01(b)(1)] without using NMLS. \n(d) \nThe application required by [Section
    6.01(b)(1)] shall include information \nrequired by [Section 5.04] for any new

    "dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a", "title": "[PDF] CSBS Money Transmission Modernization
    Act", "extraction_state": "complete", "selected_passages": [{"unit_id": "p000022",
    "start": 0, "end": 2612, "page_number": 22, "section_label": null, "body_hash":
    "175b57e812c71a8532569030d2db7113b5adc94e61bd9922dc0fee5d833c2748", "path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000022.md",
    "text": "22 \n \n(e) \nWhen an application for acquisition of control under this
    [Section 6.01] \nappears to include all the items and address all of the matters
    that are required, the application shall \nbe considered complete and the [Commissioner]
    shall promptly notify the applicant in a record of \nthe date on which the application
    was determined to be complete and:15 \n \n(1) \nThe [Commissioner] shall approve
    or deny the application within 60 \ndays after the completion date; or \n(2) \nif
    the application is not approved or denied within 60 days after the \ncompletion
    date: \n(A) \nthe application is approved; and \n(B) \nthe person, or group of
    persons acting in concert, are not \nprohibited from acquiring control. \n(3)
    \nThe [Commissioner] may for good cause extend the application \nperiod. \n(f)
    \nA determination by the [Commissioner] that an application is complete and \nis
    accepted for processing means only that the application, on its face, appears
    to include all of the \nitems and address all of the matters that are required,
    and is not an assessment of the substance of \nthe application or of the sufficiency
    of the information provided. \n(g) \nWhen an application is filed and considered
    complete under [Section \n6.01(e)], the [Commissioner] shall investigate the financial
    condition and responsibility, financial \nand business experience, character,
    and general fitness of the person, or group of persons acting in \nconcert, seeking
    to acquire control. The [Commissioner] shall approve an acquisition of control
    \npursuant to this [Section 6.01] if the [Commissioner] finds that all of the
    following conditions have \nbeen fulfilled: \n(1) \nThe requirements of subsections
    (b) and (d) have been met, as \napplicable; and \n(2) \nthe financial condition
    and responsibility, financial and business \nexperience, competence, character,
    and general fitness of the person, or group of persons \nacting in concert, seeking
    to acquire control; and the competence, experience, character, \nand general fitness
    of the key individuals and persons that would be in control of the \nlicensee
    after the acquisition of control indicate that it is in the interest of the public
    to \npermit the person, or group of persons acting in concert, to control the
    licensee. \n(h) \nIf an applicant avails itself or is otherwise subject to a multistate
    licensing \n \n15 Commentary: NMLS will accommodate and streamline the process
    of communicating when applications are \nreceived and when states consider them
    to have been complete. The intent of this Act is for the application period to
    \nbegin on the day an application is determined to be complete.\n"}], "support_state":
    "retrieved", "url": "https://www.csbs.org/sites/default/files/2023-02/CSBS%20Money%20Transmission%20Modernization%20Act.pdf",

    "source_hash": "175b57e812c71a8532569030d2db7113b5adc94e61bd9922dc0fee5d833c2748",
    "source_label": "[PDF] CSBS Money Transmission Modernization Act — Page 22, characters
    0–2612", "unit_id": "p000022", "locator": "Page 22, characters 0–2612", "available_excerpt":
    "22 \n \n(e) \nWhen an application for acquisition of control under this [Section
